1.124.s:
brahmovāca..
vakṣyāmyahaṃ te punareva diṃḍe sūryasya sarvapravarapradhānam..
vyomnaḥ paraṃ tiṣṭhati yastu magnaḥ sa mucyate rudra ihāpi diṃḍī..1..
1.124.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच॥
वक्ष्याम्यहं ते पुनरेव दिंडे सूर्यस्य सर्वप्रवरप्रधानम्॥
व्योम्नः परं तिष्ठति यस्तु मग्नः स मुच्यते रुद्र इहापि दिंडी॥1॥

1.124.s:
sthitvā purā brahmaśiraḥ kilāsau pragṛhya tattasya śiraḥkapālam..
tato hyasāvāśramamuttamaṃ śivo bahūdakaiḥ puṣpaphalaiḥ samṛddham .. 2 ..
1.124.d:
स्थित्वा पुरा ब्रह्मशिरः किलासौ प्रगृह्य तत्तस्य शिरःकपालम्॥
ततो ह्यसावाश्रममुत्तमं शिवो बहूदकैः पुष्पफलैः समृद्धम् ॥ 2 ॥
1.124.m:
Formerly, having severed Brahmā's head and seized the skull of that head of his,
Śiva then [went] to an excellent hermitage rich in copious waters, flowers, and fruits.

1.124.s:
nagno yadā dāruvane munīnāṃ dṛṣṭvā ca taṃ bhaikṣyacaraṃ sureśam ..
yoṣitsutāḥ saṃkṣubhitāstu sarve jagmurharaṃ taṃ munayaḥ sutuṣṭāḥ .. ..
sa hanyamāno munimukhyasaṃghairgṛhītaloṣṭairṛṣidaṃḍakāṣṭhaiḥ ..
vihāya diṃḍiḥ sa tu tānsurarṣīṃstato raverlokamathājagāma .. 4 ..
1.124.d:
नग्नो यदा दारुवने मुनीनां दृष्ट्वा च तं भैक्ष्यचरं सुरेशम् ॥
योषित्सुताः संक्षुभितास्तु सर्वे जग्मुर्हरं तं मुनयः सुतुष्टाः ॥ ॥
स हन्यमानो मुनिमुख्यसंघैर्गृहीतलोष्टैरृषिदंडकाष्ठैः ॥
विहाय दिंडिः स तु तान्सुरर्षींस्ततो रवेर्लोकमथाजगाम ॥ 4 ॥
1.124.m:
When, naked, in the pine forest of the sages, seeing him wandering for alms, that lord of gods—
the women and children were agitated, but the sages, highly pleased, approached Hara.
Being struck by the hosts of foremost sages with clods of earth they had seized and with sages' wooden staffs,
he, Diṇḍi, left those divine seers and went from there to the realm of the Sun.

1.124.s:
āgacchamānaṃ pramathāstamūcurdeveśa nityaṃ bhramase kimartham ..
sa prāha tānpāpavimocanārthamaṭāmi tīrthāni surālayāṃśca .. 5 ..
1.124.d:
आगच्छमानं प्रमथास्तमूचुर्देवेश नित्यं भ्रमसे किमर्थम् ॥
स प्राह तान्पापविमोचनार्थमटामि तीर्थानि सुरालयांश्च ॥ 5 ॥
1.124.m:
As he approached, the Pramathas said to him, 'O lord of gods, why do you wander constantly?'
He said to them, 'To free myself from sin, I roam holy places and abodes of the gods.'

1.124.s:
te bhūya ūcuḥ pramathāstamevamatraiva tiṣṭhasva raveḥ purastāt ..
śuddhiṃ tavaiṣa prakariṣyatīti śuddhastato yāsyasi rudralokam .. 6 ..
1.124.d:
ते भूय ऊचुः प्रमथास्तमेवमत्रैव तिष्ठस्व रवेः पुरस्तात् ॥
शुद्धिं तवैष प्रकरिष्यतीति शुद्धस्ततो यास्यसि रुद्रलोकम् ॥ 6 ॥
1.124.m:
Those Pramathas said to him again, 'Stand right here before the Sun!
He will bring about your purification; purified thereby, you will go to the realm of Rudra.'

1.124.s:
ityevamuktaḥ pramathaistu rudrastatraiva tasthau ravitoṣaṇāya ..
nagno jaṭī muṣṭikapālapāṇī rūpeṇa caivāpratimastriloke .. 7 ..
1.124.d:
इत्येवमुक्तः प्रमथैस्तु रुद्रस्तत्रैव तस्थौ रवितोषणाय ॥
नग्नो जटी मुष्टिकपालपाणी रूपेण चैवाप्रतिमस्त्रिलोके ॥ 7 ॥
1.124.m:
Having been spoken to thus by the Pramathas, Rudra stayed right there to propitiate the Sun,
naked, with matted hair, a fist-sized skull in hand, matchless in form throughout the three worlds.

1.124.s:
uktaḥ sa tuṣṭena tataḥ savitrā prītosmi devāgamanāttavāham ..
maddarśanādeva bhavānviśuddho diṃḍīti nāmnā bhavitāsi loke .. 8 ..
1.124.d:
उक्तः स तुष्टेन ततः सवित्रा प्रीतोस्मि देवागमनात्तवाहम् ॥
मद्दर्शनादेव भवान्विशुद्धो दिंडीति नाम्ना भवितासि लोके ॥ 8 ॥
1.124.m:
He was then addressed by the pleased Savitṛ: 'I am delighted by your coming, O god.
Merely by the sight of me you are purified; you shall be known in the world by the name Diṇḍin.'

1.124.s:
aṣṭādaśaite pramathāstu bhānoścaturdaśānye tu rave rathasthāḥ ..
he devate dvau ca ṛṣipradhānau gaṃdharvasarpāvapi tāvadeva .. 9 ..
1.124.d:
अष्टादशैते प्रमथास्तु भानोश्चतुर्दशान्ये तु रवे रथस्थाः ॥
हे देवते द्वौ च ऋषिप्रधानौ गंधर्वसर्पावपि तावदेव ॥ 9 ॥
1.124.m:
These eighteen Pramathas of the Sun and fourteen others reside on the Sun's chariot;
two deities, two chief sages, and as many Gandharvas and serpents;

1.124.s:
yakṣau ca siddhau ca niśācarau cādityātmajāvapsarasāṃ pradhānau ..
vasaṃti te hyastamuṣaśca sūrye teṣāma śītiścaturottarā sā .. 1.124.10 ..
1.124.d:
यक्षौ च सिद्धौ च निशाचरौ चादित्यात्मजावप्सरसां प्रधानौ ॥
वसंति ते ह्यस्तमुषश्च सूर्ये तेषाम शीतिश्चतुरोत्तरा सा ॥ 1.124.10 ॥
1.124.m:
two Yakṣas, two Siddhas, two night-roamers, two sons of Āditya, and two chief Apsarases;
they dwell from sunset to dawn in the Sun; their number is eighty-four.

1.124.s: ityādidevapravarāstu sarve dhātvarthaśabdaiśca bhavaṃti siddhāḥ .. 11 ..
1.124.d: इत्यादिदेवप्रवरास्तु सर्वे धात्वर्थशब्दैश्च भवंति सिद्धाः ॥ 11 ॥
1.124.m: All these foremost attendants of the primal god are established according to the verbal roots of their names.

1.124.s:
.. ṛṣaya ūcuḥ .. ..
vistarādbrūhi me brahmanpravarāndhātuśabdajān ..
yataśca kautukaṃ brahmannasmākamiha jāyate .. 12 ..
1.124.d:
॥ ऋषय ऊचुः ॥ ॥
विस्तराद्ब्रूहि मे ब्रह्मन्प्रवरान्धातुशब्दजान् ॥
यतश्च कौतुकं ब्रह्मन्नस्माकमिह जायते ॥ 12 ॥
1.124.m:
The sages said:
Tell me in detail, O Brahman, about these foremost attendants born from the roots of words,
for curiosity has arisen in us here, O Brahman.

1.124.s:
brahmovāca .. ..
bhūyastava pravakṣyāmi daṃḍanāyakapiṃgalau ..
rājñasrauṣādayaścānye digdevā diṃḍinā saha .. 13 ..
1.124.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ॥ ॥
भूयस्तव प्रवक्ष्यामि दंडनायकपिंगलौ ॥
राज्ञस्रौषादयश्चान्ये दिग्देवा दिंडिना सह ॥ 13 ॥
1.124.m:
Brahmā said:
I will tell you again of Daṇḍanāyaka and Piṅgala,
of Rājña, Srauṣa, and others, the deities of the directions, together with Diṇḍin.

1.124.s:
mayā saha samāgamya purā devairvicāritam ..
eṣa kāruṇikaḥ sūryo yudhyate dānavaiḥ saha .. 14 ..
1.124.d:
मया सह समागम्य पुरा देवैर्विचारितम् ॥
एष कारुणिकः सूर्यो युध्यते दानवैः सह ॥ 14 ॥
1.124.m:
Formerly, having met with me, the gods reflected:
'This compassionate Sun fights with the Dānavas;

1.124.s:
te tu labdhavarā bhūtvā amātyādyā hyabhīkṣṇaśaḥ ..
ādityaṃ manyamānāste tapaṃtaṃ haṃtumudyatāḥ .. 15 ..
1.124.d:
ते तु लब्धवरा भूत्वा अमात्याद्या ह्यभीक्ष्णशः ॥
आदित्यं मन्यमानास्ते तपंतं हंतुमुद्यताः ॥ 15 ॥
1.124.m:
and they, having obtained boons, acting repeatedly as ministers and such,
regarding Āditya as merely heating, are intent on killing him.

1.124.s:
tasmātteṣāṃ vighātārthaṃ pravarāśca bhavāmahe ..
asmābhiḥ pratiruddhāste na drakṣyaṃti divākaram .. 16 ..
1.124.d:
तस्मात्तेषां विघातार्थं प्रवराश्च भवामहे ॥
अस्माभिः प्रतिरुद्धास्ते न द्रक्ष्यंति दिवाकरम् ॥ 16 ॥
1.124.m:
Therefore, for their repulse, we shall become foremost attendants;
blocked by us, they will not see the Sun.'

1.124.s:
saṃmaṃtryaivaṃ tataḥ skaṃdo vāmapārśve raveḥ sthitaḥ ..
daṃḍanāyakasaṃjñastu sarvalokasya sa prabhuḥ .. .. 17 ..
1.124.d:
संमंत्र्यैवं ततः स्कंदो वामपार्श्वे रवेः स्थितः ॥
दंडनायकसंज्ञस्तु सर्वलोकस्य स प्रभुः ॥ ॥ 17 ॥
1.124.m:
Having consulted thus, Skanda then stood on the left side of the Sun,
known as Daṇḍanāyaka, the lord of all the world.

1.124.s:
uktaśca sa tadārkeṇa tvaṃ prajādaṃḍanāyakaḥ ..
daṃḍanītikaro yasmāttasmāttvaṃ daṃḍanāyakaḥ .. 18 ..
1.124.d:
उक्तश्च स तदार्केण त्वं प्रजादंडनायकः ॥
दंडनीतिकरो यस्मात्तस्मात्त्वं दंडनायकः ॥ 18 ॥
1.124.m:
And he was then told by the Sun: 'You are the leader of punishment for creatures;
because you apply the policy of punishment, you are therefore Daṇḍanāyaka.'

1.124.s:
likhate yaḥ prajānāṃ ca sukṛtaṃ yacca duṣkṛtam ..
agnirdakṣiṇapārśve tu piṃgalatvātsa piṃgalaḥ .. 19 ..
1.124.d:
लिखते यः प्रजानां च सुकृतं यच्च दुष्कृतम् ॥
अग्निर्दक्षिणपार्श्वे तु पिंगलत्वात्स पिंगलः ॥ 19 ॥
1.124.m:
He who records the good deeds and evil deeds of creatures
is Agni on the right side; and because he is reddish-brown, he is Piṅgala.

1.124.s:
āśvinau cāpi sūryasya pārśvayorubhayoḥ sthitau ..
aśvarūpātsamupannau tena tāvaśvinau surau .. 1.124.20 ..
1.124.d:
आश्विनौ चापि सूर्यस्य पार्श्वयोरुभयोः स्थितौ ॥
अश्वरूपात्समुपन्नौ तेन तावश्विनौ सुरौ ॥ 1.124.20 ॥
1.124.m:
And the two Aśvins stand on both flanks of the Sun;
they arose from the form of a horse, therefore they are the two gods, the Aśvins.

1.124.s:
dvārapālau smṛtau tasya rājñaḥ śreṣṭhau mahābalau ..
kārttikeyaḥ smṛto rājñaḥ śreṣṭhaścāpi haraḥ smṛtaḥ .. 21 ..
1.124.d:
द्वारपालौ स्मृतौ तस्य राज्ञः श्रेष्ठौ महाबलौ ॥
कार्त्तिकेयः स्मृतो राज्ञः श्रेष्ठश्चापि हरः स्मृतः ॥ 21 ॥
1.124.m:
His two doorkeepers are known as the kings, the best, possessed of great strength;
Kārttikeya is known as the king, and Hara is also known as the best.

1.124.s:
rājṛdīptau smṛto dhāturnakārastasya pratyayaḥ ..
surasenāpatitvena sa yasmāddīpyate sadā ..
tasmātsa kārtikeyastu nāmnā rājña iti smṛtaḥ .. 22 ..
1.124.d:
राजृदीप्तौ स्मृतो धातुर्नकारस्तस्य प्रत्ययः ॥
सुरसेनापतित्वेन स यस्माद्दीप्यते सदा ॥
तस्मात्स कार्तिकेयस्तु नाम्ना राज्ञ इति स्मृतः ॥ 22 ॥

1.124.s:
sru gatau ca smṛto dhāturyasya sa pratyayaḥ smṛtaḥ ..
gacchatīti rahastasmātparyāyātsrauṣa ucyate .. 23 ..
1.124.d:
स्रु गतौ च स्मृतो धातुर्यस्य स प्रत्ययः स्मृतः ॥
गच्छतीति रहस्तस्मात्पर्यायात्स्रौष उच्यते ॥ 23 ॥
1.124.m:
The verbal root *sru* is handed down in the sense of going, and *sa* is considered its suffix;
he moves secretly, and therefore by this synonym he is called Srauṣa.

1.124.s:
prathamaṃ yadbhaveddvāraṃ dharmārthābhyāṃ samāśritam ..
tatraitau saṃsthitau devau lokapūjyau dvijottamāḥ .. 24 ..
1.124.d:
प्रथमं यद्भवेद्द्वारं धर्मार्थाभ्यां समाश्रितम् ॥
तत्रैतौ संस्थितौ देवौ लोकपूज्यौ द्विजोत्तमाः ॥ 24 ॥
1.124.m:
At the first gate, which is associated with righteousness and prosperity,
these two deities, revered by the worlds, stand, O best of twice-born.

1.124.s:
dvitīyāyāṃ tu kakṣāyāmapradhṛṣṭau vyavasthitau ..
pakṣipretādhipau nāmnā smṛtau kalmāṣapakṣiṇau .. 25 ..
1.124.d:
द्वितीयायां तु कक्षायामप्रधृष्टौ व्यवस्थितौ ॥
पक्षिप्रेताधिपौ नाम्ना स्मृतौ कल्माषपक्षिणौ ॥ 25 ॥
1.124.m:
In the second court stand two invincible ones,
the lords of birds and pretas, known by name as Kalmāṣa and Pakṣin.

1.124.s:
varṇasya śabalatvācca yamaḥ kalmāṣa ucyate ..
pakṣāvasyeti yaḥ pakṣī garuḍaḥ parikīrtitaḥ .. 26 ..
1.124.d:
वर्णस्य शबलत्वाच्च यमः कल्माष उच्यते ॥
पक्षावस्येति यः पक्षी गरुडः परिकीर्तितः ॥ 26 ॥
1.124.m:
Because his colour is mottled, Yama is called Kalmāṣa;
he who has wings is Pakṣin, who is proclaimed to be Garuḍa.

1.124.s:
sthito dakṣiṇata tasya daṃḍahastasamanvitaḥ ..
uttareṇa sthito'rkasya kuberaśca vināyakaḥ .. 27 ..
1.124.d:
स्थितो दक्षिणत तस्य दंडहस्तसमन्वितः ॥
उत्तरेण स्थितोऽर्कस्य कुबेरश्च विनायकः ॥ 27 ॥
1.124.m:
Standing to his right with a staff in hand [is Yama];
to the north of the Sun stand Kubera and Vināyaka.

1.124.s:
kubero dhanado jñeyo hastirūpo vināyakaḥ ..
kutsayā kupyatā śaptaṃ kuśarīramajāyata ..
kuberaḥ kuśarīratvātsa nāmnā dhanadaḥ smṛtaḥ .. 28 ..
1.124.d:
कुबेरो धनदो ज्ञेयो हस्तिरूपो विनायकः ॥
कुत्सया कुप्यता शप्तं कुशरीरमजायत ॥
कुबेरः कुशरीरत्वात्स नाम्ना धनदः स्मृतः ॥ 28 ॥

1.124.s:
nāyakaḥ sarvasattvānāṃ tena nāyaka ucyate ..
vividhaṃ nayate yasmātsa tu tasmādvināyakaḥ .. 29 ..
1.124.d:
नायकः सर्वसत्त्वानां तेन नायक उच्यते ॥
विविधं नयते यस्मात्स तु तस्माद्विनायकः ॥ 29 ॥
1.124.m: He is the leader of all living beings; therefore, he is called Nāyaka. / And because he leads in various ways, he is Vināyaka.

1.124.s:
raivataścaiva diṃḍiśca tau raveḥ pūrvataḥ sthitau ..
tato diṃḍiḥ smṛto rudro revatastanayo raveḥ .. 1.124.30 ..
1.124.d:
रैवतश्चैव दिंडिश्च तौ रवेः पूर्वतः स्थितौ ॥
ततो दिंडिः स्मृतो रुद्रो रेवतस्तनयो रवेः ॥ 1.124.30 ॥
1.124.m: And Raivata and Ḍiṇḍi stand to the east of the Sun. / From this, Ḍiṇḍi is understood as Rudra, and Revata as the Sun’s son.

1.124.s:
plutaṃ gacchatyasau yasmātsarvalokanamaskṛtaḥ ..
revṛplavagatau dhātū revatastena sa smṛtaḥ ..31..
1.124.d:
प्लुतं गच्छत्यसौ यस्मात्सर्वलोकनमस्कृतः ॥
रेवृप्लवगतौ धातू रेवतस्तेन स स्मृतः ॥31॥
1.124.m: Because he, bowed to by all the worlds, moves with leaps— / the roots rev and plu signify 'to jump'—he is therefore remembered as Revata.

1.124.s:
ḍīṅgatāvasya vai dhātordiṃḍiśabdo nipātyate ..
ḍayate'sau sadā diṃḍī tena diṃḍī prakīrtitaḥ .. 32 ..
1.124.d:
डीङ्गतावस्य वै धातोर्दिंडिशब्दो निपात्यते ॥
डयतेऽसौ सदा दिंडी तेन दिंडी प्रकीर्तितः ॥ 32 ॥
1.124.m: Indeed, from the verbal root ḍīṅ, meaning 'to fly', the word ḍiṇḍi is derived as an irregular form. / He constantly flies, hence he is proclaimed as Ḍiṇḍī.

1.124.s:
ityete pravarāḥ proktā dhātvarthā naigamaiḥ śubhaiḥ ..
eṣāṃ saṃkṣepato bhūyaḥ saṃkhyāṃ vo nigadāmi vai .. 33 ..
1.124.d:
इत्येते प्रवराः प्रोक्ता धात्वर्था नैगमैः शुभैः ॥
एषां संक्षेपतो भूयः संख्यां वो निगदामि वै ॥ 33 ॥
1.124.m: Thus these foremost root-meanings have been declared by auspicious Vedic sages. / Again, I shall now relate their number to you in brief.

1.124.s:
aśvinau tau tato jñeyau daṃḍanāyakapiṃgalau ..
tau sūryadvārapau jñeyau rājñasrauṣau tataḥ smṛtau .. 34 ..
1.124.d:
अश्विनौ तौ ततो ज्ञेयौ दंडनायकपिंगलौ ॥
तौ सूर्यद्वारपौ ज्ञेयौ राज्ञस्रौषौ ततः स्मृतौ ॥ 34 ॥
1.124.m: Next are to be known the two Aśvins, Daṇḍanāyaka and Piṅgala; / they are to be known as the Sun’s doorkeepers, and then are remembered as Rājñī and Srauṣā.

1.124.s:
revataścaiva diṃḍiśca ityete pravarā mayā ..
aṣṭādaśa samā khyātāḥ saṃkṣepātsaṃkhyayā mayā .. 35 ..
1.124.d:
रेवतश्चैव दिंडिश्च इत्येते प्रवरा मया ॥
अष्टादश समा ख्याताः संक्षेपात्संख्यया मया ॥ 35 ॥
1.124.m: And Revata and Ḍiṇḍi: thus these eighteen foremost ones / have been declared by me in equal measure, counted in summary.

1.124.s:
ityebhirnāmabhistvanye dānavānāṃ jighāṃsayā ..
parivārya sthitāḥ sūryaṃ nānāpraharaṇāyudhāḥ .. 36 ..
1.124.d:
इत्येभिर्नामभिस्त्वन्ये दानवानां जिघांसया ॥
परिवार्य स्थिताः सूर्यं नानाप्रहरणायुधाः ॥ 36 ॥
1.124.m: Others, bearing various striking weapons, / stand surrounding the Sun under these names with the desire to slay the Dānavas.

1.124.s:
sarūpāścānyarūpāśca virūpāḥ kāmarūpiṇaḥ ..
parivārya sthitāḥ sūryaṃ garuḍaśca mahābalaḥ .. 37 ..
1.124.d:
सरूपाश्चान्यरूपाश्च विरूपाः कामरूपिणः ॥
परिवार्य स्थिताः सूर्यं गरुडश्च महाबलः ॥ 37 ॥
1.124.m: Bearing similar forms, other forms, deformed, or changing shape at will, / and the mighty Garuḍa—they stand surrounding the Sun.

1.124.s:
dhāturdiviti vai prokto krīḍāyāṃ sa tu ucyate ..
krīḍaṃte divi vai yasmāttasmātte daivatāḥ smṛtāḥ .. 38 ..
1.124.d:
धातुर्दिविति वै प्रोक्तो क्रीडायां स तु उच्यते ॥
क्रीडंते दिवि वै यस्मात्तस्मात्ते दैवताः स्मृताः ॥ 38 ॥
1.124.m: The verbal root div is indeed stated; it is said to mean 'to play'. / Because they play in heaven, they are therefore remembered as deities.

1.124.s:
ṛco yajūṃṣi sāmāni yānyuktānīha vai mayā ..
nānārūpaiḥ sthitānyeva ravestāni sama ntataḥ .. 39 ..
1.124.d:
ऋचो यजूंषि सामानि यान्युक्तानीह वै मया ॥
नानारूपैः स्थितान्येव रवेस्तानि सम न्ततः ॥ 39 ॥
1.124.m: The Ṛg, Yajus, and Sāma verses that have been spoken here by me / stand in varied forms all around the Sun.

1.124.s:
.. sumaṃturuvāca .. ..
ityevamuktavānbrahmā ṛṣīṇāṃ pṛcchatāṃ purā ..
te śrutvārādhya deveśaṃ saṃsiddhā divi saṃsthitāḥ .. 1.124.40 ..
1.124.d:
॥ सुमंतुरुवाच ॥ ॥
इत्येवमुक्तवान्ब्रह्मा ऋषीणां पृच्छतां पुरा ॥
ते श्रुत्वाराध्य देवेशं संसिद्धा दिवि संस्थिताः ॥ 1.124.40 ॥
1.124.m: Sumantu said: / Thus Brahmā spoke long ago to the inquiring sages. / Having heard this and worshipped the lord of the gods, they attained perfection and took their place in heaven.

1.124.s: iti śrībhaviṣye mahāpurāṇe brāhme parvaṇi saptamīkalpe brahmarṣisaṃvāde pravaravarṇanaṃ nāma caturviṃśatyuttaraśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 124 .. .. cha .. ..
1.124.d: इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराणे ब्राह्मे पर्वणि सप्तमीकल्पे ब्रह्मर्षिसंवादे प्रवरवर्णनं नाम चतुर्विंशत्युत्तरशततमोऽध्यायः ॥ 124 ॥ ॥ छ ॥ ॥
1.124.m: Thus ends the one hundred twenty-fourth chapter, entitled 'Description of the Foremost Retinue', in the dialogue between Brahmā and the sages, in the Saptamīkalpa of the Brāhmaparvan in the glorious Bhaviṣya Mahāpurāṇa.

1.125.s:
.. śatānīka uvāca .. ..
yadetaddṛśyate vyoma sūryasya purato dvija ..
taducyate kimātmā ca kathaṃbhūtaśca kathyatām .. 1 ..
1.125.d:
॥ शतानीक उवाच ॥ ॥
यदेतद्दृश्यते व्योम सूर्यस्य पुरतो द्विज ॥
तदुच्यते किमात्मा च कथंभूतश्च कथ्यताम् ॥ 1 ॥
1.125.m: Śatānīka said: / O twice-born one, this sky which is seen before the Sun— / of what nature is that which is spoken of, and of what kind is it? Please tell.

1.125.s:
.. sumaṃturuvāca .. ..
haṃta vyoma pravakṣyāmi sūryapraharaṇaṃ śubham ..
yadātmakaṃ hi yatproktaṃ yathā vasaṃti devatāḥ .. 2 ..
1.125.d:
॥ सुमंतुरुवाच ॥ ॥
हंत व्योम प्रवक्ष्यामि सूर्यप्रहरणं शुभम् ॥
यदात्मकं हि यत्प्रोक्तं यथा वसंति देवताः ॥ 2 ॥
1.125.m: Sumantu said: / Indeed, I shall describe the auspicious sky-weapon of the Sun, / of what essence it is declared to be, and how the deities reside there.

1.125.s:
purastācca catuḥśṛṃgaṃ tadvyomāyatanaṃ raveḥ ..
vyomaśabdaṃ catuḥśṛṃgaṃ sarvadevamayaṃ ca yat .. 3 ..
1.125.d:
पुरस्ताच्च चतुःशृंगं तद्व्योमायतनं रवेः ॥
व्योमशब्दं चतुःशृंगं सर्वदेवमयं च यत् ॥ 3 ॥
1.125.m: And in the front is that four-pinnacled sky-abode of the Sun, / which is termed 'the sky', has four peaks, and consists of all the gods.

1.125.s:
gairikārṇavasaṃbhūtaṃ yadaṃtargarbhamāśritam ..
tatrotpannamidaṃ vyoma kalervyoma mahī smṛtā .. 4 ..
1.125.d:
गैरिकार्णवसंभूतं यदंतर्गर्भमाश्रितम् ॥
तत्रोत्पन्नमिदं व्योम कलेर्व्योम मही स्मृता ॥ 4 ॥
1.125.m: Arisen from the red-ochre ocean, resting in its inner womb, / there this sky was generated; the earth is remembered as the sky of the Kali age.

1.125.s:
varuṇasya yathā pāśo huṅkāro vedhaso yathā ..
viṣṇoścāpi yathā cakraṃ triśūlaṃ tryaṃbakasya ca ..5..
1.125.d:
वरुणस्य यथा पाशो हुङ्कारो वेधसो यथा ॥
विष्णोश्चापि यथा चक्रं त्रिशूलं त्र्यंबकस्य च ॥5॥
1.125.m: As is the noose of Varuṇa, as is the huṅkāra of the Creator, / as is the discus of Viṣṇu, and the trident of Tryambaka,

1.125.s:
indrasya ca yathā vajraṃ tathā vyoma raveḥ smṛtam ..
tasminvyomni trayastriṃśatkrīḍanto yajñiyāḥ surāḥ .. 6 ..
1.125.d:
इन्द्रस्य च यथा वज्रं तथा व्योम रवेः स्मृतम् ॥
तस्मिन्व्योम्नि त्रयस्त्रिंशत्क्रीडन्तो यज्ञियाः सुराः ॥ 6 ॥
1.125.m: and as is the thunderbolt of Indra, so the sky is remembered as the Sun's weapon. / In that sky, thirty-three sacrificial gods disport themselves:

1.125.s:
haraśca varṣaśuddhaśca tryaṃbakaścāparājitaḥ ..
vṛṣākapiśca śaṃbhuśca kapardī raivatastathā ..
īśvaro bhuvanaścaite rudrā ekādaśa smṛtāḥ .. 7 ..
1.125.d:
हरश्च वर्षशुद्धश्च त्र्यंबकश्चापराजितः ॥
वृषाकपिश्च शंभुश्च कपर्दी रैवतस्तथा ॥
ईश्वरो भुवनश्चैते रुद्रा एकादश स्मृताः ॥ 7 ॥
1.125.m: Hara, Varṣaśuddha, Tryambaka, Aparājita, / Vṛṣākapi, Śambhu, Kapardin, Raivata, / Īśvara, and Bhuvana—these are remembered as the eleven Rudras.

1.125.s:
ādityānāṃ ca nāmāni viṣṇoścakrasya dīyatām ..
aryamā ca tathā mitro bhago'tha varuṇastathā .. 8 ..
1.125.d:
आदित्यानां च नामानि विष्णोश्चक्रस्य दीयताम् ॥
अर्यमा च तथा मित्रो भगोऽथ वरुणस्तथा ॥ 8 ॥
1.125.m: And let the names of the Ādityas, belonging to the discus of Viṣṇu, be proclaimed: / Aryaman, Mitra, Bhaga, and Varuṇa,

1.125.s:
vivasvāntsavitā caiva pūṣā tvaṣṭā tathaiva ca ..
aṃśo bhagaścātitejā ādityā dvādaśa smṛtāḥ .. 9 ..
1.125.d:
विवस्वान्त्सविता चैव पूषा त्वष्टा तथैव च ॥
अंशो भगश्चातितेजा आदित्या द्वादश स्मृताः ॥ 9 ॥
1.125.m: Vivasvat, Savitṛ, Pūṣan, Tvaṣṭṛ, / Aṃśa, and the exceedingly splendid Bhaga—these are remembered as the twelve Ādityas.

1.125.s:
dhruvo dharaśca somaśca āpaścaivā'nilo'nalaḥ .
pratyūṣaśca prabhātaśca vasavo'ṣṭau prakīrtitāḥ . . 1.125.10
1.125.d:
ध्रुवो धरश्च सोमश्च आपश्चैवाऽनिलोऽनलः ।
प्रत्यूषश्च प्रभातश्च वसवोऽष्टौ प्रकीर्तिताः ॥ 1.125.10
1.125.m: Dhruva, Dhara, Soma, Āpa, Anila, Anala, / Pratyūṣa, and Prabhāta are proclaimed as the eight Vasus.

1.125.s:
nāsatyaścaiva dasraśca smṛtau dvāvaśvināvubhau .
viśvedevānpravakṣyāmi nāmatastānnibodhata . . 11
1.125.d:
नासत्यश्चैव दस्रश्च स्मृतौ द्वावश्विनावुभौ ।
विश्वेदेवान्प्रवक्ष्यामि नामतस्तान्निबोधत ॥ 11
1.125.m: Nāsatya and Dasra are remembered as the two Aśvins. / I shall declare the Viśvedevas; learn them by name:

1.125.s:
kraturdakṣo vasuḥ satyaḥ kālakāmau dhṛtiḥ kuruḥ .
śaṅkumātro vāmanaśca viśvedevā daśa smṛtāḥ . . 12
1.125.d:
क्रतुर्दक्षो वसुः सत्यः कालकामौ धृतिः कुरुः ।
शङ्कुमात्रो वामनश्च विश्वेदेवा दश स्मृताः ॥ 12
1.125.m: Kratu, Dakṣa, Vasu, Satya, Kāla, Kāma, Dhṛti, Kuru, / Śaṅkumātra, and Vāmana are remembered as the ten Viśvedevas.

1.125.s:
vartamānā ime devā bhaviṣyānantare śṛṇu .
yamaśca tuṣitāścaiva1 vasavo2 vaśavartinaḥ . . 13
1.125.d:
वर्तमाना इमे देवा भविष्यानन्तरे शृणु ।
यमश्च तुषिताश्चैव1 वसवो2 वशवर्तिनः ॥ 13
1.125.m: These are the present gods; hear now about those in future intervals: / the Yamas, Tuṣitas, and Vasus under their control,

1.125.s:
satyāśca bhūtarajasaḥ sādhyāśca tadanantarā .
ṣaṭsu manvantareṣvevaṃ devā dvādaśadvādaśa3 . .
pārāvatāstathā cānye te hyāsaṃstuṣitaiḥ saha . . 14
1.125.d:
सत्याश्च भूतरजसः साध्याश्च तदनन्तरा ।
षट्सु मन्वन्तरेष्वेवं देवा द्वादशद्वादश3 ॥
पारावतास्तथा चान्ये ते ह्यासंस्तुषितैः सह ॥ 14
1.125.m: the Satyas, the Bhūtarajases, and next to them the Sādhyas; / thus in six Manu intervals there are twelve gods in each, / and others, the Pārāvatas, who were together with the Tuṣitas.

1.125.s:
sādhyāndevānpravakṣyāmi nāmatastānnibodha me .
mano'numantā prāṇaśca naro nārāyaṇastathā . . 15
1.125.d:
साध्यान्देवान्प्रवक्ष्यामि नामतस्तान्निबोध मे ।
मनोऽनुमन्ता प्राणश्च नरो नारायणस्तथा ॥ 15
1.125.m: I shall declare the Sādhya gods; learn them from me by name: / Manas, Anumantṛ, Prāṇa, Nara, Nārāyaṇa,

1.125.s:
vṛttilambo manuścaiva samo4 dharmaśca vīryavān .
vittasvāmī prabhuścaiva sādhyā dvādaśa kīrtitāḥ . . 16
1.125.d:
वृत्तिलम्बो मनुश्चैव समो4 धर्मश्च वीर्यवान् ।
वित्तस्वामी प्रभुश्चैव साध्या द्वादश कीर्तिताः ॥ 16
1.125.m: Vṛttilamba, Manu, Sama, and the valiant Dharma, / Vittasvāmin, and Prabhu are proclaimed as the twelve Sādhyas.

1.125.s:
ete yajñabhujo devāḥ sarvalokeṣu pūjitāḥ .
ādityāmeva te dhīra kaśyapasyātmajāḥ smṛtāḥ . . 17
1.125.d:
एते यज्ञभुजो देवाः सर्वलोकेषु पूजिताः ।
आदित्यामेव ते धीर कश्यपस्यात्मजाः स्मृताः ॥ 17
1.125.m: These sacrifice-enjoying gods are worshipped in all the worlds. / In the solar line, O wise one, they are remembered as the sons of Kaśyapa.

1.125.s:
viśve ca vasavaḥ sādhyā vijñeyā dharmasūnavaḥ .
evaṃ dharmasutaḥ somastṛtīyo vasuriṣyate . . 18
1.125.d:
विश्वे च वसवः साध्या विज्ञेया धर्मसूनवः ।
एवं धर्मसुतः सोमस्तृतीयो वसुरिष्यते ॥ 18
1.125.m: The Viśvedevas, Vasus, and Sādhyas are to be known as sons of Dharma. / Thus Soma, the third Vasu, is considered the son of Dharma.

1.125.s:
dharmo'pi brahmaṇaḥ putraḥ purāṇe niścayaṃ gataḥ .
atha cendrānvasūṃścaiva nāmabhiśca nibodha me . . 19
1.125.d:
धर्मोऽपि ब्रह्मणः पुत्रः पुराणे निश्चयं गतः ।
अथ चेन्द्रान्वसूंश्चैव नामभिश्च निबोध मे ॥ 19
1.125.m: Dharma is also established in the Purāṇa as the son of Brahmā. / Now learn from me the Indras and Vasus by their names.

1.125.s:
svāyambhuvo manuḥ pūrvaḥ tataḥ svārociṣaḥ smṛtaḥ .
uttamastāmasaścaiva raivataścākṣuṣastathā . . 1.125.20
1.125.d:
स्वायम्भुवो मनुः पूर्वः ततः स्वारोचिषः स्मृतः ।
उत्तमस्तामसश्चैव रैवतश्चाक्षुषस्तथा ॥ 1.125.20
1.125.m: First was Svāyambhuva Manu, then Svārociṣa is remembered, / Uttama, Tāmasa, Raivata, and Cākṣuṣa.

1.125.s:
ityete ṣaḍatikrāntāḥ saptamaḥ sāmprato manuḥ .
vaivasvateti vijñeyo bhaviṣyāḥ sapta cāpare . . 21
1.125.d:
इत्येते षडतिक्रान्ताः सप्तमः साम्प्रतो मनुः ।
वैवस्वतेति विज्ञेयो भविष्याः सप्त चापरे ॥ 21
1.125.m: These six have passed away; the seventh is the present Manu, / who is to be known as Vaivasvata; and seven others are future.

1.125.s:
eṣāmādyorkasāvarṇirbrahmasāvarṇireva ca .
tasmācca bhavasāvarṇirdharmasāvarṇirityuta . . 22
1.125.d:
एषामाद्योर्कसावर्णिर्ब्रह्मसावर्णिरेव च ।
तस्माच्च भवसावर्णिर्धर्मसावर्णिरित्युत ॥ 22
1.125.m: The first of these is Arkasāvarṇi, then Brahmasāvarṇi, / and after that Bhavasāvarṇi, and Dharmasāvarṇi,

1.125.s:
pañcamo dakṣasāvarṇiḥ sāvarṇiḥ5 pañca kīrtitāḥ .
raucyo bhauvyaśca dvāvanyāvityete manavaḥ smṛtāḥ . . 23
1.125.d:
पञ्चमो दक्षसावर्णिः सावर्णिः5 पञ्च कीर्तिताः ।
रौच्यो भौव्यश्च द्वावन्यावित्येते मनवः स्मृताः ॥ 23
1.125.m: and the fifth is Dakṣasāvarṇi—these five Sāvarṇis are proclaimed; / Raucya and Bhauvya are the two others: thus these Manus are remembered.

1.125.s:
indrastu viṣṇubhugjñeyo vidyutistadanantaram .
vibhuḥ prabhuścaiva śikhī tathaiva ca manojavaḥ . . 24
1.125.d:
इन्द्रस्तु विष्णुभुग्ज्ञेयो विद्युतिस्तदनन्तरम् ।
विभुः प्रभुश्चैव शिखी तथैव च मनोजवः ॥ 24
1.125.m: Indra is to be known as Viṣṇubhuj, and after that Vidyuti, / Vibhu, Prabhu, Śikhin, and Manojava,

1.125.s:
ojasvī sāmpratisvindro balirbhāvyastataḥ param .
adbhutastridivaścaiva daśamastvindra ucyate . . 25
1.125.d:
ओजस्वी साम्प्रतिस्विन्द्रो बलिर्भाव्यस्ततः परम् ।
अद्भुतस्त्रिदिवश्चैव दशमस्त्विन्द्र उच्यते ॥ 25
1.125.m: and Ojasvin is the present Indra; Bali is to be the next after him; / then Adbhuta, and Tridiva is said to be the tenth Indra,

1.125.s:
susāttvikaśca1 kīrtiśca śatadhāmā2 divaspatiḥ .
iti bhūtā bhaviṣyāśca indrā jñeyāścaturdaśa . . 26
1.125.d:
सुसात्त्विकश्च1 कीर्तिश्च शतधामा2 दिवस्पतिः ।
इति भूता भविष्याश्च इन्द्रा ज्ञेयाश्चतुर्दश ॥ 26
1.125.m: Susāttvika, Kīrti, Śatadhāman, and Divaspati. / Thus fourteen past and future Indras are to be known.

1.125.s:
kaśyapo'trirvaśiṣṭhaśca bharadvājaśca gautamaḥ .
viśvāmitro jamadagniḥ saptaite ṛṣayaḥ smṛtāḥ . . 27
1.125.d:
कश्यपोऽत्रिर्वशिष्ठश्च भरद्वाजश्च गौतमः ।
विश्वामित्रो जमदग्निः सप्तैते ऋषयः स्मृताः ॥ 27
1.125.m: Kaśyapa, Atri, Vasiṣṭha, Bharadvāja, Gautama, / Viśvāmitra, and Jamadagni—these are remembered as the seven sages.

1.125.s:
ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi maruto'gniparigrahān .
pravahothāvahaścaiva udvahaḥ saṃvahastathā . . 28
1.125.d:
अतः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि मरुतोऽग्निपरिग्रहान् ।
प्रवहोथावहश्चैव उद्वहः संवहस्तथा ॥ 28
1.125.m: Henceforth I shall declare the Maruts, who are attendants of fire: / Pravaha, then Āvaha, Udvaha, Saṃvaha,

1.125.s:
vivaho nivahaścaiva parivāhastathaiva ca .
antarikṣacarā3 hyete pṛthaṅmārgavisāriṇaḥ . . 29
1.125.d:
विवहो निवहश्चैव परिवाहस्तथैव च ।
अन्तरिक्षचरा3 ह्येते पृथङ्मार्गविसारिणः ॥ 29
1.125.m: Vivaha, Nivaha, and likewise Parivāha; / for these roam in the atmosphere, spreading along separate paths.

1.125.s:
sūryo'gniśca śucirnāmnā vaidyutaḥ pāvakaḥ smṛtaḥ .
nirmanthaḥ pavamāno'gnistrayaḥ proktā imegnayaḥ . . 1.125.30
1.125.d:
सूर्योऽग्निश्च शुचिर्नाम्ना वैद्युतः पावकः स्मृतः ।
निर्मन्थः पवमानोऽग्निस्त्रयः प्रोक्ता इमेग्नयः ॥ 1.125.30
1.125.m:
The solar fire is named Śuci, the lightning [fire] is known as Pāvaka,
and the fire produced by friction is Pavamāna; these three fires are declared.

1.125.s:
agnīnāṃ putrapautrāstu catvāriṃśattathaiva tu .
marutāmapi sarveṣāṃ vijñeyāḥ saptasaptakāḥ . . 31
1.125.d:
अग्नीनां पुत्रपौत्रास्तु चत्वारिंशत्तथैव तु ।
मरुतामपि सर्वेषां विज्ञेयाः सप्तसप्तकाः ॥ 31
1.125.m:
The sons and grandsons of the fires are forty;
and all the Maruts should be known as seven groups of seven.

1.125.s:
ṛtuḥ saṃvatsaro'hyagnirṛtavastasya jajñire .
ṛtuputrāśca vai pañca iti sargaḥ sanātanaḥ . . 32
1.125.d:
ऋतुः संवत्सरोऽह्यग्निरृतवस्तस्य जज्ञिरे ।
ऋतुपुत्राश्च वै पञ्च इति सर्गः सनातनः ॥ 32
1.125.m:
The season is the year, fire indeed; the seasons were born from it.
And the sons of the seasons are five; such is the eternal creation.

1.125.s:
saṃvatsarastu prathamo dvitīyaḥ parivatsaraḥ .
idvatsarastṛtīyastu caturthastvanuvatsaraḥ . . 33
1.125.d:
संवत्सरस्तु प्रथमो द्वितीयः परिवत्सरः ।
इद्वत्सरस्तृतीयस्तु चतुर्थस्त्वनुवत्सरः ॥ 33
1.125.m:
The first is Saṃvatsara, the second Parivatsara,
the third is Idvatsara, and the fourth is Anuvatsara.

1.125.s:
pañcamo vatsarasteṣāmityevaṃ pañca te smṛtāḥ .
teṣu saṃvatsaro hyagniḥ sūryastu parivatsaraḥ . . 34
1.125.d:
पञ्चमो वत्सरस्तेषामित्येवं पञ्च ते स्मृताः ।
तेषु संवत्सरो ह्यग्निः सूर्यस्तु परिवत्सरः ॥ 34
1.125.m:
The fifth of them is Vatsara; thus these five are remembered.
Among them, Saṃvatsara is fire, and Parivatsara is the Sun;

1.125.s:
soma idvatsarasteṣāṃ vāyuścaivānuvatsaraḥ .
rudrastu vatsaro jñeyaḥ pañcaitā ' yugadevatāḥ . . 35
1.125.d:
सोम इद्वत्सरस्तेषां वायुश्चैवानुवत्सरः ।
रुद्रस्तु वत्सरो ज्ञेयः पञ्चैता ' युगदेवताः ॥ 35
1.125.m:
Soma is their Idvatsara, and Vāyu is Anuvatsara;
Rudra should be known as Vatsara: these are the five deities of the [five-year] cycle.

1.125.s:
ārtavā pitaro jñeyā ye jātāḥ ṛtusūnavaḥ .
pitāmahāstu vijñeyāḥ pañcābdā brahmaṇaḥ sutāḥ . . 36
1.125.d:
आर्तवा पितरो ज्ञेया ये जाताः ऋतुसूनवः ।
पितामहास्तु विज्ञेयाः पञ्चाब्दा ब्रह्मणः सुताः ॥ 36
1.125.m:
The sons of the seasons who were born are to be known as the Ārtava ancestors;
and the five years, sons of Brahmā, are to be known as the grandfathers.

1.125.s:
saumyā barhiṣadaścaiva agniṣvāttāśca ye trayaḥ .
ete vai pitarasteṣāṃ ye jīvatpitṛkā narāḥ . . 37
1.125.d:
सौम्या बर्हिषदश्चैव अग्निष्वात्ताश्च ये त्रयः ।
एते वै पितरस्तेषां ये जीवत्पितृका नराः ॥ 37
1.125.m:
The Saumyas, the Barhiṣads, and the Agniṣvāttas are the three [groups];
these indeed are the ancestors for those men whose fathers are still living.

1.125.s:
ādityaścaiva somaśca lohitāṅgo budhastathā .
bṛhaspatiśca śukraśca tathā helisutaśca yaḥ . . 38
1.125.d:
आदित्यश्चैव सोमश्च लोहिताङ्गो बुधस्तथा ।
बृहस्पतिश्च शुक्रश्च तथा हेलिसुतश्च यः ॥ 38
1.125.m:
Āditya, Soma, Lohitāṅga, and Budha,
Bṛhaspati, Śukra, and he who is the son of Heli [the Sun],

1.125.s:
uparāgaḥ śikhī cobhau navaite nu grahāḥ smṛtāḥ .
trailokyasya tvime nityaṃ bhāvābhāvanivedakāḥ . . 39
1.125.d:
उपरागः शिखी चोभौ नवैते नु ग्रहाः स्मृताः ।
त्रैलोक्यस्य त्विमे नित्यं भावाभावनिवेदकाः ॥ 39
1.125.m:
along with both Uparāga [Rāhu] and Śikhin [Ketu]—these nine are remembered as the planets;
these perpetually announce the fortune and misfortune of the three worlds.

1.125.s:
ādityaścaiva somaśca dvāvetau maṇḍalagrahau .
rāhuśchāyāgrahasteṣāṃ śeṣāstārā grahāḥ smṛtāḥ . .1.125.4 0
nakṣatrādhipatiḥ somo graharājo divākaraḥ .
paṭhyate cāgnirāditya udakaścandramāḥ smṛtaḥ . . 41
1.125.d:
आदित्यश्चैव सोमश्च द्वावेतौ मण्डलग्रहौ ।
राहुश्छायाग्रहस्तेषां शेषास्तारा ग्रहाः स्मृताः ॥1.125.4 0
नक्षत्राधिपतिः सोमो ग्रहराजो दिवाकरः ।
पठ्यते चाग्निरादित्य उदकश्चन्द्रमाः स्मृतः ॥ 41

1.125.s:
ādityaḥ paṭhyate brahmā viṣṇusteṣāṃ tu candramāḥ .
maheśvarastu vijñeyastṛtīyastārakagrahaḥ . . 42
1.125.d:
आदित्यः पठ्यते ब्रह्मा विष्णुस्तेषां तु चन्द्रमाः ।
महेश्वरस्तु विज्ञेयस्तृतीयस्तारकग्रहः ॥ 42
1.125.m:
Āditya is recited as Brahmā, and the Moon among them as Viṣṇu;
and Maheśvara is to be known as the third, the star-planets.

1.125.s:
kaśyapasya sutaḥ sūryaḥ somo dharmasutaḥ smṛtaḥ .
devāsuragurū dvau tu nāmatastau1 mahāgrahau . . 43
1.125.d:
कश्यपस्य सुतः सूर्यः सोमो धर्मसुतः स्मृतः ।
देवासुरगुरू द्वौ तु नामतस्तौ1 महाग्रहौ ॥ 43
1.125.m:
Sūrya is the son of Kaśyapa, Soma is recorded as the son of Dharma;
the two teachers of gods and demons are celebrated by name as great planets.

1.125.s:
prajāpatisutāvetāvubhau śukrabṛhaspatī .
budhaḥ somātmajaḥ śrīmāñchanī ravisutaḥ smṛtaḥ . . 44
1.125.d:
प्रजापतिसुतावेतावुभौ शुक्रबृहस्पती ।
बुधः सोमात्मजः श्रीमाञ्छनी रविसुतः स्मृतः ॥ 44
1.125.m:
Both of these, Śukra and Bṛhaspati, are sons of Prajāpati;
splendid Budha is the son of Soma, and Śani is recorded as the son of Ravi.

1.125.s:
siṃhikāyāḥ suto rāhuḥ ketustu brahmaṇaḥ sutaḥ .
sarveṣāṃ ca grahāṇāṃ hi adhastāccarate raviḥ . . 45
1.125.d:
सिंहिकायाः सुतो राहुः केतुस्तु ब्रह्मणः सुतः ।
सर्वेषां च ग्रहाणां हि अधस्ताच्चरते रविः ॥ 45
1.125.m:
Rāhu is the son of Siṃhikā, while Ketu is the son of Brahmā;
and Ravi travels beneath all the planets.

1.125.s:
tato dūraṃ smṛtaṃ tāvadvidhornakṣatramaṇḍalam .
nakṣatrebhyaḥ kujabudhau śvetāhvastadanantaram . . 46
1.125.d:
ततो दूरं स्मृतं तावद्विधोर्नक्षत्रमण्डलम् ।
नक्षत्रेभ्यः कुजबुधौ श्वेताह्वस्तदनन्तरम् ॥ 46
1.125.m:
Above that is recorded the sphere of the Moon's asterisms at such a distance;
above the asterisms are Mars and Mercury, and next is he named Śveta [Venus].

1.125.s:
tasmānmāheśvaraścorddhvaṃ dhiṣaṇastadanantaram .
kṛṣṇaścordhvaṃ tatastasmādatha citraśikhaṇḍijaḥ . . 47
1.125.d:
तस्मान्माहेश्वरश्चोर्द्ध्वं धिषणस्तदनन्तरम् ।
कृष्णश्चोर्ध्वं ततस्तस्मादथ चित्रशिखण्डिजः ॥ 47
1.125.m:
Above that is Māheśvara [Jupiter], and next is Dhiṣaṇa;
then above that is Kṛṣṇa [Saturn], and after that the offspring of the Citraśikhaṇḍins [the Seven Sages].

1.125.s:
eṣāmeva kramaḥ proktāścāsaktaṃ tridivaṃ dhruve .
ādityanilayo rāhuḥ kadācitsomamārgagaḥ . . 48
1.125.d:
एषामेव क्रमः प्रोक्ताश्चासक्तं त्रिदिवं ध्रुवे ।
आदित्यनिलयो राहुः कदाचित्सोममार्गगः ॥ 48
1.125.m:
This order of them has been declared, and heaven is fixed to Dhruva;
Rāhu has his abode in the Sun, and sometimes he travels in the path of the Moon.

1.125.s:
sūryamaṇḍalasaṃsthastu1 śikhī sarpati sarvadā .
navayojanasāhasro vistāro bhārgavasya2 tu . . 49
1.125.d:
सूर्यमण्डलसंस्थस्तु1 शिखी सर्पति सर्वदा ।
नवयोजनसाहस्रो विस्तारो भार्गवस्य2 तु ॥ 49
1.125.m:
Resting within the Sun's disk, Śikhin creeps continuously;
the diameter of Bhārgava is nine thousand yojanas.

1.125.s:
dviguṇaḥ sūryavistārādvistāraḥ śaninaḥ smṛtaḥ .
triguṇaṃ3 maṃḍalaṃ jñeyaṃ nākṣatraṃ vistarādvidhoḥ . . 1.125.50
1.125.d:
द्विगुणः सूर्यविस्ताराद्विस्तारः शनिनः स्मृतः ।
त्रिगुणं3 मंडलं ज्ञेयं नाक्षत्रं विस्तराद्विधोः ॥ 1.125.50
1.125.m:
The diameter of Saturn is recorded as twice the diameter of the Sun;
the asterism sphere should be known as three times the diameter of the Moon.

1.125.s:
nakṣatramaṇḍalāttatra pādahīno bṛhaspatiḥ .
bṛhaspateḥ pādahīnaḥ śukroṅgāraka eva hi . . 51
1.125.d:
नक्षत्रमण्डलात्तत्र पादहीनो बृहस्पतिः ।
बृहस्पतेः पादहीनः शुक्रोङ्गारक एव हि ॥ 51
1.125.m:
Bṛhaspati is one quarter less than the sphere of asterisms;
Śukra is one quarter less than Bṛhaspati, and so is Aṅgāraka [Mars].

1.125.s:
vistāro maṇḍalānāṃ tu pādahīnastayorbudhaḥ .
budhatulyāni ṛkṣāṇi sarvaṛkṣāṇi yāni tu . . 52
1.125.d:
विस्तारो मण्डलानां तु पादहीनस्तयोर्बुधः ।
बुधतुल्यानि ऋक्षाणि सर्वऋक्षाणि यानि तु ॥ 52
1.125.m:
Budha is one quarter less in diameter than the disks of those two;
all the lunar asterisms are equal in size to Budha.

1.125.s:
yojanānyardhamātrāṇi tebhyo hrasvaṃ na vidyate .
rāhuḥ sūryapramāṇaśca kadācitsomasannibhaḥ . . 53
1.125.d:
योजनान्यर्धमात्राणि तेभ्यो ह्रस्वं न विद्यते ।
राहुः सूर्यप्रमाणश्च कदाचित्सोमसन्निभः ॥ 53
1.125.m:
They measure merely half a yojana; none is found smaller than them;
Rāhu is equal in measure to the Sun, and sometimes he resembles the Moon.

1.125.s:
nakṣatragrahamānastu1 ketustvaniyataḥ smṛtaḥ .
avijñātagatiścaiva cañcalatvannarādhipa . . 54
1.125.d:
नक्षत्रग्रहमानस्तु1 केतुस्त्वनियतः स्मृतः ।
अविज्ञातगतिश्चैव चञ्चलत्वन्नराधिप ॥ 54
1.125.m:
The size of Ketu as a star-planet is remembered as irregular,
and his course is unknown because of his restlessness, O king.

1.125.s:
tathālakṣitarūpastu bahurūpadharo hi saḥ .
bhūrlokaḥ pṛthivī proktā antarikṣaṃ bhuvaḥ smṛtam . . 55
1.125.d:
तथालक्षितरूपस्तु बहुरूपधरो हि सः ।
भूर्लोकः पृथिवी प्रोक्ता अन्तरिक्षं भुवः स्मृतम् ॥ 55
1.125.m:
Indeed, his form is imperceptible, for he assumes many forms.
Bhūrloka is said to be the earth, and the intermediate region is remembered as Bhuvas.

1.125.s:
svarlokastridivaṃ jñeyaṃ śeṣādūrdhvaṃ yathākramam .
bhūpatistu sadā tvagnistenāsau bhūpatiḥ smṛtaḥ . . 56
1.125.d:
स्वर्लोकस्त्रिदिवं ज्ञेयं शेषादूर्ध्वं यथाक्रमम् ।
भूपतिस्तु सदा त्वग्निस्तेनासौ भूपतिः स्मृतः ॥ 56
1.125.m:
Svarloka is to be known as heaven, and above the rest in regular order;
fire is always the lord of the earth, therefore he is remembered as Bhūpati.

1.125.s:
vāyurnabhaspatistena tathā sūryo divaspatiḥ .
gandharvāpsarasaścaiva guhyakāḥ siddharākṣasāḥ . .57
1.125.d:
वायुर्नभस्पतिस्तेन तथा सूर्यो दिवस्पतिः ।
गन्धर्वाप्सरसश्चैव गुह्यकाः सिद्धराक्षसाः ॥57
1.125.m:
By that [rule] Vāyu is lord of the atmosphere, and likewise the Sun is lord of heaven.
Gandharvas, apsarases, guhyakas, siddhas, and rākṣasas

1.125.s:
bhūrlokavāsinaḥ sarve antarikṣacarāñchṛṇu .
marutaḥ saptamaskaṃdhe rudrāstatraiva cāśvinau . .58
1.125.d:
भूर्लोकवासिनः सर्वे अन्तरिक्षचराञ्छृणु ।
मरुतः सप्तमस्कंधे रुद्रास्तत्रैव चाश्विनौ ॥58
1.125.m:
are all inhabitants of Bhūrloka; now hear of those who move in the intermediate region:
the Maruts in the seventh wind-level, and there too the Rudras and the two Aśvins,

1.125.s:
ādityā vasavaḥ sarve tathaiva ca gavāṃ gaṇāḥ .
caturthe tu maharloke vasante kalpavāsinaḥ . .5 9
prajānāṃ patibhiḥ sarveḥ sahitāḥ kurunandana .
janaloke pañcame ca vasante bhūmidāḥ sadā . . 1.125.60
1.125.d:
आदित्या वसवः सर्वे तथैव च गवां गणाः ।
चतुर्थे तु महर्लोके वसन्ते कल्पवासिनः ॥5 9
प्रजानां पतिभिः सर्वेः सहिताः कुरुनन्दन ।
जनलोके पञ्चमे च वसन्ते भूमिदाः सदा ॥ 1.125.60
1.125.m:
all the Ādityas and the Vasus, and likewise the herds of cattle.
In the fourth realm, Maharloka, dwell the inhabitants of the kalpa,
together with all the lords of creatures, O scion of the Kurus;
and in Janaloka, the fifth, givers of land dwell perpetually,

1.125.s:
ṛtuḥ sanatkumārādyā vairājabhra tathāśrayāḥ .
satyastu saptame loke hyapunarmārgagāminām . . 61
1.125.d:
ऋतुः सनत्कुमाराद्या वैराजभ्र तथाश्रयाः ।
सत्यस्तु सप्तमे लोके ह्यपुनर्मार्गगामिनाम् ॥ 61
1.125.m:
along with the season, Sanatkumāra and the others who take refuge in the luminous sphere of Vairāja;
and the realm of Satya is the seventh world for those who go on the path of non-return.

1.125.s:
brahmalokaḥ samākhyāto hyapratīghātalakṣaṇaḥ .
itihāsavido yatra krīḍante kurunandana . . 62
1.125.d:
ब्रह्मलोकः समाख्यातो ह्यप्रतीघातलक्षणः ।
इतिहासविदो यत्र क्रीडन्ते कुरुनन्दन ॥ 62
1.125.m:
It is proclaimed as Brahmaloka, characterised by unobstructedness,
where knowers of traditional history disport themselves, O scion of the Kurus,

1.125.s:
śṛṇvanti ca purāṇāni ye sadā bhīmanaṃdana .
mahītalātsahasrāṇāṃ śatādūrdhvaṃ divākaraḥ . . 63
1.125.d:
शृण्वन्ति च पुराणानि ये सदा भीमनंदन ।
महीतलात्सहस्राणां शतादूर्ध्वं दिवाकरः ॥ 63
1.125.m:
and those who continually listen to the Purāṇas, O son of Bhīma.
The Sun is a hundred thousand [yojanas] above the surface of the earth.

1.125.s:
śatayojanakoṭyastu1 bhūmerūrdhvaṃ dhruvaḥ sthitaḥ .
tato viṃśatilakṣastu trailokyotsedha ucyate . . 64
1.125.d:
शतयोजनकोट्यस्तु1 भूमेरूर्ध्वं ध्रुवः स्थितः ।
ततो विंशतिलक्षस्तु त्रैलोक्योत्सेध उच्यते ॥ 64
1.125.m:
Dhruva is situated a hundred crore yojanas above the earth;
the height of the three worlds is said to be twenty hundred thousand beyond that.

1.125.s:
dviguṇaistu sahasraistu yojanānāṃ śateṣu ca .
lokāṃtaramatho caivaṃ dhruvādūrdhvaṃ vidhīyate . . 65
1.125.d:
द्विगुणैस्तु सहस्रैस्तु योजनानां शतेषु च ।
लोकांतरमथो चैवं ध्रुवादूर्ध्वं विधीयते ॥ 65
1.125.m:
By twice that number of thousands and hundreds of yojanas,
another world above Dhruva is thus ordained.

1.125.s:
devadānavagandharvā yakṣarākṣasapannagāḥ .
bhūtā vidyādharāścaiva aṣṭau te devayonayaḥ . . 66
1.125.d:
देवदानवगन्धर्वा यक्षराक्षसपन्नगाः ।
भूता विद्याधराश्चैव अष्टौ ते देवयोनयः ॥ 66
1.125.m:
Gods, dānavas, gandharvas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, and serpents,
ghosts, and vidyādharas—these are the eight classes of divine beings.

1.125.s:
yasminvyomni tvime lokāḥ sapta vai sampratiṣṭhitāḥ .
marutaḥ pitaro hyete tasminnevāgnayo grahāḥ . . 67
1.125.d:
यस्मिन्व्योम्नि त्विमे लोकाः सप्त वै सम्प्रतिष्ठिताः ।
मरुतः पितरो ह्येते तस्मिन्नेवाग्नयो ग्रहाः ॥ 67
1.125.m:
In that very space where these seven worlds are established,
the Maruts, the ancestors, the fires, and the planets reside.

1.125.s:
yāstvapyetāḥ samākhyātā mayāṣṭau devayonayaḥ .
mūrtāścāmūrtayaścaiva sarvāstā vyomni saṃsthitāḥ . . 6 8
evaṃvidhamidaṃ vyoma sarvavyomamayaṃ smṛtam .
sarvadevamayaṃ caiva sarvagrahamayaṃ tathā . . 69
1.125.d:
यास्त्वप्येताः समाख्याता मयाष्टौ देवयोनयः ।
मूर्ताश्चामूर्तयश्चैव सर्वास्ता व्योम्नि संस्थिताः ॥ 6 8
एवंविधमिदं व्योम सर्वव्योममयं स्मृतम् ।
सर्वदेवमयं चैव सर्वग्रहमयं तथा ॥ 69
1.125.m:
And these eight classes of divine beings that have been spoken of by me,
both corporeal and incorporeal, are all situated in space.
Such is this space, remembered as consisting of all space,
consisting of all deities, and consisting of all planets.

1.125.s:
tasmādyo hyarcayedvyoma tena sarve'rcitāḥ surāḥ .
tasmātsarvaprayatnena śubhārthī vyoma cārcayet . . 1.125.70
1.125.d:
तस्माद्यो ह्यर्चयेद्व्योम तेन सर्वेऽर्चिताः सुराः ।
तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन शुभार्थी व्योम चार्चयेत् ॥ 1.125.70
1.125.m:
Therefore, whoever worships space has worshipped all the gods;
therefore, one who desires what is auspicious should worship space with every effort.

1.125.s:
yastvarcate sadā vyoma bhaktyā śraddhāsamanvitaḥ .
vṛṣadhvajasado rājansa gacchennātra saṃśayaḥ . . 71
vyomamāhātmyavarṇanam
1.125.d:
यस्त्वर्चते सदा व्योम भक्त्या श्रद्धासमन्वितः ।
वृषध्वजसदो राजन्स गच्छेन्नात्र संशयः ॥ 71
व्योममाहात्म्यवर्णनम्
1.125.m:
He who always worships space with devotion, endowed with faith,
goes to the realm of the Bull-bannered [Śiva], O king; of this there is no doubt.
Description of the Praise of Space

1.126.s:
sumanturuvāca
ākāśaṃ khaṃ diśo vyoma antarikṣaṃ nabho'mbaram .
puṣkaraṃ gaganaṃ merurvipulaṃ ca bilaṃ tathā . . 1
1.126.d:
सुमन्तुरुवाच
आकाशं खं दिशो व्योम अन्तरिक्षं नभोऽम्बरम् ।
पुष्करं गगनं मेरुर्विपुलं च बिलं तथा ॥ 1
1.126.m:
Sumantu said:
Ākāśa, kha, diś, vyoman, antarikṣa, nabhas, ambara,
puṣkara, gagana, meru, vipula, bila,

1.126.s:
āpochidraṃ tathā śūnyaṃ tamo vai rodasī tathā .
nāmānyetāni te vyomnaḥ kīrtitāni mahīpate . . 2
1.126.d:
आपोछिद्रं तथा शून्यं तमो वै रोदसी तथा ।
नामान्येतानि ते व्योम्नः कीर्तितानि महीपते ॥ 2
1.126.m:
āpas, chidra, śūnya, tamas, and rodasī:
these names of space have been declared to you, O king.

1.126.s:
lavaṇakṣīradadhyamlaghṛtamadhvikṣavastathā .
svādūdakaśca saptaite samudrāḥ parikīrtitāḥ . . 3
1.126.d:
लवणक्षीरदध्यम्लघृतमध्विक्षवस्तथा ।
स्वादूदकश्च सप्तैते समुद्राः परिकीर्तिताः ॥ 3
1.126.m: Salt water, milk, curd, sour gruel, clarified butter, wine, and sugarcane juice, / and fresh water: these seven oceans are proclaimed.

1.126.s:
himavānhemakūṭaśca niṣadho nīla eva ca .
śvetaśca śṛṅgavāṃścaiva ṣaḍete varṣaparvatāḥ . .4
1.126.d:
हिमवान्हेमकूटश्च निषधो नील एव च ।
श्वेतश्च शृङ्गवांश्चैव षडेते वर्षपर्वताः ॥4
1.126.m: Himavān, Hemakūṭa, Niṣadha, Nīla, / Śveta, and Śṛṅgavān: these six are the boundary mountains of the continents.

1.126.s:
madhyasaṃsthastathaiteṣāṃ mahārājataparvataḥ .
māhendrī cāpyathāgneyī yāmyā ca nairṛtī tathā . . 5
1.126.d:
मध्यसंस्थस्तथैतेषां महाराजतपर्वतः ।
माहेन्द्री चाप्यथाग्नेयी याम्या च नैरृती तथा ॥ 5
1.126.m: And situated in their center is the great golden mountain [Meru]. / Then the cities of Indra, Agni, Yama, and Nirṛti,

1.126.s:
vāruṇī cātha vāyavyā saumyaiśānī tathaiva ca .
etāḥ puryastu devānāṃ tathopari samāśritāḥ . . 6
1.126.d:
वारुणी चाथ वायव्या सौम्यैशानी तथैव च ।
एताः पुर्यस्तु देवानां तथोपरि समाश्रिताः ॥ 6
1.126.m: of Varuṇa, Vāyu, Soma, and Īśāna— / these cities of the gods are situated above it.

1.126.s:
pṛthivyāṃ tu sthito vīra lokālokastu parvataḥ .
tataścaṇḍakapālaṃ tu tasmāttatparatastu yaḥ . . 7
1.126.d:
पृथिव्यां तु स्थितो वीर लोकालोकस्तु पर्वतः ।
ततश्चण्डकपालं तु तस्मात्तत्परतस्तु यः ॥ 7
1.126.m: O hero, the mountain Lokāloka stands on the earth. / Beyond that is the shell of the cosmic egg, and beyond that what follows:

1.126.s:
tato'gnirvāyurākāśaṃ tato bhūtādirucyate .
tato mahānahaṅkāraḥ prakṛtiḥ puruṣastataḥ . . 8
1.126.d:
ततोऽग्निर्वायुराकाशं ततो भूतादिरुच्यते ।
ततो महानहङ्कारः प्रकृतिः पुरुषस्ततः ॥ 8
1.126.m: then fire, wind, space; then the origin of the elements is declared; / then the great principle [Mahat], egoism, primal nature [Prakṛti], and then the spirit [Puruṣa].

1.126.s:
puruṣādīśvaro śreya īśvareṇāvrṛtaṃ jagat .
īśvaro bhagavanbhānustenedaṃ pūritaṃ jagat . . 9
1.126.d:
पुरुषादीश्वरो श्रेय ईश्वरेणाव्रृतं जगत् ।
ईश्वरो भगवन्भानुस्तेनेदं पूरितं जगत् ॥ 9
1.126.m: Beyond the spirit, Īśvara is to be known; by Īśvara the universe is pervaded. / Īśvara is the blessed Sun; by him this universe is filled,

1.126.s:
sahasrāṃśurmahātejāścaturbāhurmahābalaḥ .
ūrdhvamapyatha lokāstu prāṅmayā ye prakīrtitāḥ . . 1.126.10
1.126.d:
सहस्रांशुर्महातेजाश्चतुर्बाहुर्महाबलः ।
ऊर्ध्वमप्यथ लोकास्तु प्राङ्मया ये प्रकीर्तिताः ॥ 1.126.10
1.126.m: the thousand-rayed, immensely radiant, four-armed, of great might. / And the upper worlds which were proclaimed by me before,

1.126.s:
bhūyastānsampravakṣyāmi aṇḍāvaraṇakārakān .
bhūrlokastubhuvarlokastṛtīyaḥ parikīrtitaḥ . . 11
1.126.d:
भूयस्तान्सम्प्रवक्ष्यामि अण्डावरणकारकान् ।
भूर्लोकस्तुभुवर्लोकस्तृतीयः परिकीर्तितः ॥ 11
1.126.m: I shall declare them again, which form the coverings of the egg: / Bhūrloka, Bhuvarloka, and the third is declared [Svarloka],

1.126.s:
maharjanastapaḥ satyaḥ saptalokāḥ prakīrtitāḥ .
1tatastavaṃḍakapālaṃ tu tasmācca parastapaḥ . . 12
1.126.d:
महर्जनस्तपः सत्यः सप्तलोकाः प्रकीर्तिताः ।
1ततस्तवंडकपालं तु तस्माच्च परस्तपः ॥ 12
1.126.m: Maharloka, Janaloka, Tapoloka, and Satyaloka—seven worlds are declared. / Beyond them is the shell of the cosmic egg, and beyond that is the supreme [enveloping principle]:

1.126.s:
tato'gnirvāyurākāśaṃ tato bhūtādirucyate .
tato mahānpradhānaśca prakṛtipuruṣastataḥ . . 13
1.126.d:
ततोऽग्निर्वायुराकाशं ततो भूतादिरुच्यते ।
ततो महान्प्रधानश्च प्रकृतिपुरुषस्ततः ॥ 13
1.126.m: then fire, wind, space; then the origin of the elements is declared; / then the great principle and Pradhāna, and then Prakṛti and Puruṣa.

1.126.s:
puruṣādīśvaro jñeya īśvareṇāvṛtaṃ jagat .
bhūmeradhastātsaptaiva lokānabhimatāñchṛṇu . . 14
1.126.d:
पुरुषादीश्वरो ज्ञेय ईश्वरेणावृतं जगत् ।
भूमेरधस्तात्सप्तैव लोकानभिमताञ्छृणु ॥ 14
1.126.m: Beyond the spirit, Īśvara is to be known; by Īśvara the universe is pervaded. / Hear now of the seven chosen worlds beneath the earth:

1.126.s:
talaṃ sutalapātāle talātalaṃ tathātalam .
vitalaṃ ca kuruśreṣṭha saptamaṃ ca rasātalam . . 15
1.126.d:
तलं सुतलपाताले तलातलं तथातलम् ।
वितलं च कुरुश्रेष्ठ सप्तमं च रसातलम् ॥ 15
1.126.m: Tala, Sutala, Pātāla, Talātala, Atala, / Vitala, O best of the Kurus, and the seventh, Rasātala.

1.126.s:
tato'gnirvāyurākāśaṃ tato bhūtādirucyate .
tato mahānpradhānaśca prakṛtiḥ puruṣastataḥ . . 16
1.126.d:
ततोऽग्निर्वायुराकाशं ततो भूतादिरुच्यते ।
ततो महान्प्रधानश्च प्रकृतिः पुरुषस्ततः ॥ 16
1.126.m: Then fire, wind, space; then the origin of the elements is declared; / then the great principle and Pradhāna, Prakṛti, and then Puruṣa.

1.126.s:
puruṣādīśvaro jñeya īśvareṇāvṛtaṃ jagat .
evaṃ meroḥ pramāṇaṃ tu sarvametatprakīrtitam . . 17
1.126.d:
पुरुषादीश्वरो ज्ञेय ईश्वरेणावृतं जगत् ।
एवं मेरोः प्रमाणं तु सर्वमेतत्प्रकीर्तितम् ॥ 17
1.126.m: Beyond Puruṣa, Īśvara is to be known; by Īśvara the universe is pervaded. / Thus all this measurement of Meru has been proclaimed.

1.126.s:
caturasraścatuḥ śṛṃgaḥ sa meruḥ kāñcanaḥ śubhaḥ .
pṛthivyāṃ saṃsthito madhye siddhagandharvasevitaḥ . . 18
1.126.d:
चतुरस्रश्चतुः शृंगः स मेरुः काञ्चनः शुभः ।
पृथिव्यां संस्थितो मध्ये सिद्धगन्धर्वसेवितः ॥ 18
1.126.m: Square, four-peaked is that auspicious golden Meru, / standing in the center of the earth, frequented by Siddhas and Gandharvas,

1.126.s:
caturbhiḥ kāñcanaiḥ śṛṃgairdivyairdivamivollikhan .
yojanānāṃ sahasrāṇi caturāśītirucchritaḥ . . 19
1.126.d:
चतुर्भिः काञ्चनैः शृंगैर्दिव्यैर्दिवमिवोल्लिखन् ।
योजनानां सहस्राणि चतुराशीतिरुच्छ्रितः ॥ 19
1.126.m: with four divine golden peaks as if scraping the sky, / eighty-four thousand yojanas in height,

1.126.s:
praviṣṭaḥ ṣoḍaśādhastādaṣṭaviṃśativistṛtaḥ .
vistārastriguṇaścāsya pariṇāhastataḥ smṛtaḥ . . 1.126.20
1.126.d:
प्रविष्टः षोडशाधस्तादष्टविंशतिविस्तृतः ।
विस्तारस्त्रिगुणश्चास्य परिणाहस्ततः स्मृतः ॥ 1.126.20
1.126.m: penetrating sixteen [thousand] beneath, twenty-eight wide; / and its circumference is traditionally known to be three times its breadth.

1.126.s:
tasya saumanasaṃ nāma śṛṃgamekaṃ tu kāñcanam .
dvitīyaṃ padmarāgābhaṃ jyotiṣkaṃ nāma nāmataḥ . . 21
1.126.d:
तस्य सौमनसं नाम शृंगमेकं तु काञ्चनम् ।
द्वितीयं पद्मरागाभं ज्योतिष्कं नाम नामतः ॥ 21
1.126.m: One golden peak of it is called Saumanasa; / the second, ruby-colored, is called Jyotiṣka by name;

1.126.s:
tṛtīyaṃ nāmataścitraṃ sarvadevamayaṃ śubham .
caturthaṃ rājataṃ śuklaṃ candraujaskamiti smṛtam . . 22
1.126.d:
तृतीयं नामतश्चित्रं सर्वदेवमयं शुभम् ।
चतुर्थं राजतं शुक्लं चन्द्रौजस्कमिति स्मृतम् ॥ 22
1.126.m: the third is named Citra, composed of all the gods, auspicious; / the fourth is of silver, white, remembered as Candraujaska.

1.126.s:
yattu saumanasaṃ nāma śṛṃgaṃ gāṅgeyamucyate .
tadeva codayo nāmnā yatrodyandṛśyate raviḥ . . 23
1.126.d:
यत्तु सौमनसं नाम शृंगं गाङ्गेयमुच्यते ।
तदेव चोदयो नाम्ना यत्रोद्यन्दृश्यते रविः ॥ 23
1.126.m: That golden peak which is called Saumanasa / is also named Udaya, where the rising sun is seen.

1.126.s:
uttareṇa parikramya jambūdvīpaṃ divākaraḥ .
dṛśyo bhavati bhūtānāṃ śikharaṃ ca samāsthitaḥ . . 24
1.126.d:
उत्तरेण परिक्रम्य जम्बूद्वीपं दिवाकरः ।
दृश्यो भवति भूतानां शिखरं च समास्थितः ॥ 24
1.126.m: Circumambulating Jambūdvīpa by the north, the sun, / standing on the peak, becomes visible to living beings.

1.126.s:
kāñcanasya ca śailasya tejasārkasya cāhṛte .
ubhe sandhye prakāśete ātāmre pūrvapaścime . . 25
1.126.d:
काञ्चनस्य च शैलस्य तेजसार्कस्य चाहृते ।
उभे सन्ध्ये प्रकाशेते आताम्रे पूर्वपश्चिमे ॥ 25
1.126.m: Brought forth by the splendor of the golden mountain and the sun, / the two twilights, morning and evening, shine reddish.

1.126.s:
śṛṃge saumanase sūrya uttiṣṭhatyuttarāyaṇe .
jyotiṣe dakṣiṇe cāpi viṣuve madhyatastayoḥ . . 26
1.126.d:
शृंगे सौमनसे सूर्य उत्तिष्ठत्युत्तरायणे ।
ज्योतिषे दक्षिणे चापि विषुवे मध्यतस्तयोः ॥ 26
1.126.m: The sun rises on Mount Saumanasa during the northern solstice, / on Jyotiṣa during the southern, and between the two at the equinox.

1.126.s:
īśendrodriśca aiśānyāṃ tatrāgniḥ pūrvadakṣiṇe .
nairṛte'pi tato jñeyo vāyavye marutastathā . . 27
1.126.d:
ईशेन्द्रोद्रिश्च ऐशान्यां तत्राग्निः पूर्वदक्षिणे ।
नैरृतेऽपि ततो ज्ञेयो वायव्ये मरुतस्तथा ॥ 27
1.126.m: Īśāna and Indra's peak is in the northeast; there Agni is in the southeast; / then [Nirṛti] is to be known in the southwest, and in the northwest the Maruts.

1.126.s:
madhye tu kaṃjajaḥ sākṣādgrahā jyotīṃṣi caiva hi .
ādityastena rūpeṇa tasminvyomni pratiṣṭhitaḥ . . 28
1.126.d:
मध्ये तु कंजजः साक्षाद्ग्रहा ज्योतींषि चैव हि ।
आदित्यस्तेन रूपेण तस्मिन्व्योम्नि प्रतिष्ठितः ॥ 28
1.126.m: In the center is the lotus-born [Brahmā] himself, and the planets and luminaries; / in that form, the sun is established in that sky.

1.126.s:
idaṃ devamayaṃ vyoma tathā lokamayaṃ smṛtam .
pūrvakoṇasthite śṛṃge sthitaḥ śukro mahīpate . . 29
1.126.d:
इदं देवमयं व्योम तथा लोकमयं स्मृतम् ।
पूर्वकोणस्थिते शृंगे स्थितः शुक्रो महीपते ॥ 29
1.126.m: This sky is remembered as composed of the gods and composed of the worlds. / Standing on the peak in the eastern corner, O king, is Śukra;

1.126.s:
helijaścāpare jñeyo dhananāthastathāpare .
somaścāpi caturthe tu sthitaḥ śṛṃge janādhipa . . 1.126.30
1.126.d:
हेलिजश्चापरे ज्ञेयो धननाथस्तथापरे ।
सोमश्चापि चतुर्थे तु स्थितः शृंगे जनाधिप ॥ 1.126.30
1.126.m: the son of Sūrya [Śani] is to be known on the other, and on another the lord of wealth [Kubera]; / and Soma stands on the fourth peak, O ruler of people.

1.126.s:
madhye keśāsthito rājanhuṅkāraśca pinākinaḥ .
śṛṃge pūrvottare rājansthito devo vidhukṣaye1 . . 31
1.126.d:
मध्ये केशास्थितो राजन्हुङ्कारश्च पिनाकिनः ।
शृंगे पूर्वोत्तरे राजन्स्थितो देवो विधुक्षये1 ॥ 31
1.126.m: In the center stand the hairs and the roaring sound of the wielder of Pināka [Śiva]. / On the northeast peak, O king, stands the god at the waning of the moon [Śiva].

1.126.s:
tataḥ sthito mahādevo gopatirlokapūjitaḥ .
pūrvāgneyīsthite śṛṃge sthito vai śāṇḍilaḥ sutaḥ . . 32
1.126.d:
ततः स्थितो महादेवो गोपतिर्लोकपूजितः ।
पूर्वाग्नेयीस्थिते शृंगे स्थितो वै शाण्डिलः सुतः ॥ 32
1.126.m: Next stands Mahādeva, the lord of cattle, revered by the worlds. / On the peak situated in the southeast stands indeed the son of Śāṇḍila [Agni].

1.126.s:
tataḥ sthito mahātejāḥ kīnāśo helinandanaḥ .
sthito vai nairṛte śṛṃge virūpākṣo mahābalaḥ . . 33
1.126.d:
ततः स्थितो महातेजाः कीनाशो हेलिनन्दनः ।
स्थितो वै नैरृते शृंगे विरूपाक्षो महाबलः ॥ 33
1.126.m: Next stands the immensely radiant Yama, the son of the sun; / on the southwest peak stands the mighty Virūpākṣa.

1.126.s:
tasmādanantaro devaḥ sthito vai yādasāṃ patiḥ .
tataḥ sthito mahātejā vīra mitro mahābalaḥ . . 34
1.126.d:
तस्मादनन्तरो देवः स्थितो वै यादसां पतिः ।
ततः स्थितो महातेजा वीर मित्रो महाबलः ॥ 34
1.126.m: Adjacent to him stands the divine lord of aquatic creatures [Varuṇa]; / next stands the immensely radiant hero Mitra, of great power,

1.126.s:
vāyavyaṃ śṛṃgamāśritya sarvadevanamaskṛtam .
tataḥ sthito daśabalo naramāruhya bhārata . . 35
1.126.d:
वायव्यं शृंगमाश्रित्य सर्वदेवनमस्कृतम् ।
ततः स्थितो दशबलो नरमारुह्य भारत ॥ 35
1.126.m: resorting to the northwestern peak, bowed to by all the gods. / Next stands the ten-powered [Kubera], mounted on a man, O Bhārata.

1.126.s:
brahmā madhye sthito devo hyanantaścādha eva hi .
upendraśaṅkarau devau brahmaṇo'nte samāsthitau . . 36
1.126.d:
ब्रह्मा मध्ये स्थितो देवो ह्यनन्तश्चाध एव हि ।
उपेन्द्रशङ्करौ देवौ ब्रह्मणोऽन्ते समास्थितौ ॥ 36
1.126.m: In the middle stands the divine Brahmā, and Ananta indeed down below; / the gods Upendra and Śaṅkara stand near Brahmā.

1.126.s:
eṣa merustathā vyoma eṣa dharmaśca paṭhyate .
sarvadevamayaścāyaṃ merurvyoma iti smṛtaḥ . . 37
1.126.d:
एष मेरुस्तथा व्योम एष धर्मश्च पठ्यते ।
सर्वदेवमयश्चायं मेरुर्व्योम इति स्मृतः ॥ 37
1.126.m: This is Meru, and thus the sky; this is recited as Dharma. / Composed of all the gods, this Meru is remembered as the sky.

1.126.s:
tathā vedamayaścāpi paṭhyate nātra saṃśayaḥ .
śṛṃgāṇi vedāścatvāraḥ pūrvaśṛṃgādayo viduḥ . . 38
1.126.d:
तथा वेदमयश्चापि पठ्यते नात्र संशयः ।
शृंगाणि वेदाश्चत्वारः पूर्वशृंगादयो विदुः ॥ 38
1.126.m: It is also recited as composed of the Vedas; there is no doubt in this. / The wise know the peaks, beginning with the eastern peak, to be the four Vedas.

1.126.s:
iti śrībhaviṣye mahāpurāṇe brāhme parvaṇi saptamīkalpe vyomamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ
nāma ṣaḍviṃśatyadhikaśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ . 126 .
sūryaprasādavarṇanam
1.126.d:
इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराणे ब्राह्मे पर्वणि सप्तमीकल्पे व्योममाहात्म्यवर्णनं
नाम षड्विंशत्यधिकशततमोऽध्यायः । 126 ।
सूर्यप्रसादवर्णनम्
1.126.m:
Thus ends the one hundred twenty-sixth chapter, named 'Description of the Greatness of the Sky' in the Seventh Rite of the Brāhmaparvan in the glorious and great Bhaviṣyapurāṇa.
Description of the Sun's Grace

1.127.s:
śatānīka uvāca
kathamārādhitaḥ sūryaḥ sāmbenāmitatejasā .
vimuktastu kathaṃ rogairbrūhi māṃ dvijasattama . . 1
1.127.d:
शतानीक उवाच
कथमाराधितः सूर्यः साम्बेनामिततेजसा ।
विमुक्तस्तु कथं रोगैर्ब्रूहि मां द्विजसत्तम ॥ 1
1.127.m: Śatānīka said: / How was the sun worshipped by Sāmba of boundless splendor, / and how was he freed from disease? Tell me, O best of the twice-born.

1.127.s:
sumanturuvāca
sādhu pṛṣṭo'smi rājendra śṛṇu sāmbakathāṃ purā .
vistārādvacmi te sarvāṃ kathāṃ pāpavimocinīm . . 2
1.127.d:
सुमन्तुरुवाच
साधु पृष्टोऽस्मि राजेन्द्र शृणु साम्बकथां पुरा ।
विस्ताराद्वच्मि ते सर्वां कथां पापविमोचिनीम् ॥ 2
1.127.m: Sumantu said: / I am well asked, O ruler of kings! Hear the story of Sāmba in ancient times. / I shall tell you in full the whole story that delivers one from sins.

1.127.s:
purā saṃśrutya māhātmyaṃ bhāskarasya sa nāradāt .
vinayādupasaṅgamya vacaḥ pitaramabravīt . . 3
1.127.d:
पुरा संश्रुत्य माहात्म्यं भास्करस्य स नारदात् ।
विनयादुपसङ्गम्य वचः पितरमब्रवीत् ॥ 3
1.127.m: Formerly, having heard the greatness of the Sun from Nārada, / approaching his father with humility, he spoke [these] words:

1.127.s:
kaśmalenābhibhūto'smi malena vyādhinācyuta .
vaidyairoṣadhibhiścāpi na śāntirmama vidyate . . 4
1.127.d:
कश्मलेनाभिभूतोऽस्मि मलेन व्याधिनाच्युत ।
वैद्यैरोषधिभिश्चापि न शान्तिर्मम विद्यते ॥ 4
1.127.m: I am overcome by misery, by foul disease, O Acyuta; / and no relief is found for me through physicians or medicines.

1.127.s:
vanaṃ gacchāmi bhagavannanujñāṃ dātumarhasi .
śivena puṇḍarīkākṣa dhyāya māṃ puruṣottama . . 5
1.127.d:
वनं गच्छामि भगवन्ननुज्ञां दातुमर्हसि ।
शिवेन पुण्डरीकाक्ष ध्याय मां पुरुषोत्तम ॥ 5
1.127.m: I go to the forest, O Blessed One; you should grant permission. / With auspiciousness, O lotus-eyed one, think of me, O supreme among men.

1.127.s:
anujñātaḥ sa kṛṣṇena sindhoruttarakūlataḥ .
gatvā santārayāmāsa candrabhāgāṃ mahānadīm . . 6
1.127.d:
अनुज्ञातः स कृष्णेन सिन्धोरुत्तरकूलतः ।
गत्वा सन्तारयामास चन्द्रभागां महानदीम् ॥ 6
1.127.m: Permitted by Kṛṣṇa, having gone from the northern bank of the Sindhu, / he crossed the great river Candrabhāgā.

1.127.s:
tato mitravanaṃ gatvā tīrthaṃ trailokyaviśrutam .
upavāsaparaḥ sāmbaḥ śuṣko dhamanisantataḥ . . 7
1.127.d:
ततो मित्रवनं गत्वा तीर्थं त्रैलोक्यविश्रुतम् ।
उपवासपरः साम्बः शुष्को धमनिसन्ततः ॥ 7
1.127.m: Then having gone to Mitravana, the sacred place celebrated in the three worlds, / devoted to fasting, emaciated, his veins standing out,

1.127.s:
ārādhanārthaṃ sūryasya guhyaṃ stotraṃ1 jajāpa ha .
vedaiścaturbhiḥ samitaṃ purāṇāśrayabṛṃhitam . . 8
1.127.d:
आराधनार्थं सूर्यस्य गुह्यं स्तोत्रं1 जजाप ह ।
वेदैश्चतुर्भिः समितं पुराणाश्रयबृंहितम् ॥ 8
1.127.m: for the purpose of worshipping the sun, Sāmba chanted a secret hymn / equal to the four Vedas and augmented by the foundation of the Purāṇas.

1.127.s:
yadetanmaṇḍalaṃ śuklaṃ divyaṃ hyajaramavyayam .
yuktaṃ manojavairaśvairhārītairbrahmavādibhiḥ2 . . 9
1.127.d:
यदेतन्मण्डलं शुक्लं दिव्यं ह्यजरमव्ययम् ।
युक्तं मनोजवैरश्वैर्हारीतैर्ब्रह्मवादिभिः2 ॥ 9
1.127.m: This white, divine orb, unaging and imperishable, / yoked with horses swift as thought, green and proclaiming the Veda,

1.127.s:
ādireṣa1 hi bhūtānāmāditya iti saṃjñitaḥ .
trailokyacakṣurevātra paramātmā prajāpatiḥ . . 1.127.10
1.127.d:
आदिरेष1 हि भूतानामादित्य इति संज्ञितः ।
त्रैलोक्यचक्षुरेवात्र परमात्मा प्रजापतिः ॥ 1.127.10
1.127.m: he is indeed the beginning of beings, named Āditya; / he is the eye of the three worlds here, the Supreme Self, Prajāpati.

1.127.s:
eṣa vai maṇḍale hyasminpuruṣo dīpyate mahān .
eṣa viṣṇuracintyātmā brahmā caiṣa pitāmahaḥ . . 11
1.127.d:
एष वै मण्डले ह्यस्मिन्पुरुषो दीप्यते महान् ।
एष विष्णुरचिन्त्यात्मा ब्रह्मा चैष पितामहः ॥ 11
1.127.m: The great Person who shines within this orb, / he is Viṣṇu of inconceivable nature, and he is Brahmā the Grandfather;

1.127.s:
rudro mahendro varuṇa ākāśaṃ pṛthivī jalam .
vāyuḥ śaśāṅkaḥ parjanyo dhanādhyakṣo vibhāvasuḥ . . 12
1.127.d:
रुद्रो महेन्द्रो वरुण आकाशं पृथिवी जलम् ।
वायुः शशाङ्कः पर्जन्यो धनाध्यक्षो विभावसुः ॥ 12
1.127.m: he is Rudra, Mahendra, Varuṇa, space, earth, water, / wind, the moon, the rain cloud, the lord of wealth, and fire.

1.127.s:
yaṣa eṣa maṇḍale hyasmin puruṣo dīpyate mahān .
ekaḥ sākṣānmahādevo vṛtramaṇḍanibhaḥ sadā . . 13
1.127.d:
यष एष मण्डले ह्यस्मिन् पुरुषो दीप्यते महान् ।
एकः साक्षान्महादेवो वृत्रमण्डनिभः सदा ॥ 13
1.127.m: The great Person who shines within this orb, / he alone is Mahādeva in visible form, always resembling the orb of the sun.

1.127.s:
kālo hyeṣa mahābāhurnibodhotpattilakṣaṇaḥ .
ya eṣa maṇḍale hyasmiṃstejobhiḥ pūrayanmahīm . . 14
1.127.d:
कालो ह्येष महाबाहुर्निबोधोत्पत्तिलक्षणः ।
य एष मण्डले ह्यस्मिंस्तेजोभिः पूरयन्महीम् ॥ 14
1.127.m: Know him, O mighty-armed one, to be Time, whose characteristic is origin, / he who, within this orb, fills the earth with his splendours,

1.127.s:
bhrāmyate hyavyavacchinno vātairyo'mṛtalakṣaṇaḥ .
nātaḥ parataraṃ kiñcittejasā vidyate kvacit . . 15
1.127.d:
भ्राम्यते ह्यव्यवच्छिन्नो वातैर्योऽमृतलक्षणः ।
नातः परतरं किञ्चित्तेजसा विद्यते क्वचित् ॥ 15
1.127.m: who revolves uninterruptedly by the winds, whose nature is immortality; / nothing higher than him in splendour is found anywhere.

1.127.s: puṣṇāti sarvabhūtāni eṣa eva sudhāmṛtaiḥ . antasthānmlecchajātīyāṃstiryagyonigatānapi . . 16
1.127.d: पुष्णाति सर्वभूतानि एष एव सुधामृतैः । अन्तस्थान्म्लेच्छजातीयांस्तिर्यग्योनिगतानपि ॥ 16
1.127.m: He alone nourishes all beings with nectars of ambrosia, / even those residing within, outcast tribes, and those born among animals.

1.127.s:
kāruṇyātsarvabhūtāni pāsi tvaṃ ca vibhāvaso .
śvitrakuṣṭhyaṃdhabadhirānpaṃgūṃścāpi tathā vibho . . 17
1.127.d:
कारुण्यात्सर्वभूतानि पासि त्वं च विभावसो ।
श्वित्रकुष्ठ्यंधबधिरान्पंगूंश्चापि तथा विभो ॥ 17
1.127.m: Out of compassion you protect all beings, O Sun; / and also those with leucoderma, lepers, the blind, the deaf, and the lame, O all-pervading lord.

1.127.s:
prapannavatsalo deva kurute nīrujo bhavān .
cakramaṇḍalamagrāṃśca nirdhanālpāyuṣastathā . . 18
1.127.d:
प्रपन्नवत्सलो देव कुरुते नीरुजो भवान् ।
चक्रमण्डलमग्रांश्च निर्धनाल्पायुषस्तथा ॥ 18
1.127.m: Affectionate to the surrendered, O God, you make them free of disease, / as well as the foremost among the circle of provinces, the destitute, and those of short lifespan.

1.127.s:
pratyakṣadarśī tvaṃ deva samuddharasi līlayā .
kā me śaktiḥ stavaiḥ stotumārto'haṃ rogapīḍitaḥ . . 19
1.127.d:
प्रत्यक्षदर्शी त्वं देव समुद्धरसि लीलया ।
का मे शक्तिः स्तवैः स्तोतुमार्तोऽहं रोगपीडितः ॥ 19
1.127.m: Seeing directly, O God, you deliver [them] with ease. / What power have I to praise with hymns, afflicted as I am and tormented by disease?

1.127.s:
stūyase tvaṃ sadā devairbrahmaviṣṇuśivādibhiḥ .
mahendrasiddhagandharvairapsarobhiḥ saguhyakaiḥ . . 1.127.20
1.127.d:
स्तूयसे त्वं सदा देवैर्ब्रह्मविष्णुशिवादिभिः ।
महेन्द्रसिद्धगन्धर्वैरप्सरोभिः सगुह्यकैः ॥ 1.127.20
1.127.m: You are ever praised by the gods, headed by Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva, / by Mahendra, the Siddhas, the Gandharvas, along with the Apsarases and Guhyakas.

1.127.s:
stutibhiḥ kiṃ pavitrairvā tava deva samīritaiḥ .
yasya te ṛgyajuḥ sāmnāṃ tritaya maṇḍalasthitam . . 21
1.127.d:
स्तुतिभिः किं पवित्रैर्वा तव देव समीरितैः ।
यस्य ते ऋग्यजुः साम्नां त्रितय मण्डलस्थितम् ॥ 21
1.127.m: What need have you, O God, of purifying praises spoken, / you in whose orb abides the triad of the Ṛg, Yajur, and Sāma Vedas?

1.127.s:
dhyānināṃ tvaṃ paraṃ dhyānaṃ mokṣadvāraṃ ca mokṣiṇām .
anantatejasākṣobhyo hyaciṃtyāvyaktaniṣkalaḥ . . 22
1.127.d:
ध्यानिनां त्वं परं ध्यानं मोक्षद्वारं च मोक्षिणाम् ।
अनन्ततेजसाक्षोभ्यो ह्यचिंत्याव्यक्तनिष्कलः ॥ 22
1.127.m: For meditators you are the supreme meditation, and for seekers of liberation the door to liberation; / unshakeable by infinite splendour, inconceivable, unmanifest, without parts.

1.127.s:
yadayaṃ vyāhataḥ kiñcitstotre'smiñjagataḥ patiḥ .
ārtiṃ bhaktiṃ ca vijñāya tatsarvaṃ jñātumarhasi . . 23
1.127.d:
यदयं व्याहतः किञ्चित्स्तोत्रेऽस्मिञ्जगतः पतिः ।
आर्तिं भक्तिं च विज्ञाय तत्सर्वं ज्ञातुमर्हसि ॥ 23
1.127.m: If anything has been recited [amiss] in this hymn to the Lord of the world, / you ought to acknowledge it all, knowing my distress and devotion.

1.127.s:
tamuvāca tataḥ sūryaḥ prītyā jāmbavatīsutam .
prīto'smi tapasā vatse brūhi tanmāṃ yadicchasi . . 24
1.127.d:
तमुवाच ततः सूर्यः प्रीत्या जाम्बवतीसुतम् ।
प्रीतोऽस्मि तपसा वत्से ब्रूहि तन्मां यदिच्छसि ॥ 24
1.127.m: Then the Sun with affection spoke to the son of Jāmbavatī: / "I am pleased with your asceticism, dear child; tell me what you desire of me."

1.127.s:
sāmba uvāca
yadi prasanno bhagavāneṣa eva varo mama .
bhaktirbhavatu me'tyarthaṃ tvayi deva sanātana . . 25
1.127.d:
साम्ब उवाच
यदि प्रसन्नो भगवानेष एव वरो मम ।
भक्तिर्भवतु मेऽत्यर्थं त्वयि देव सनातन ॥ 25
1.127.m: Sāmba said: / "If the Blessed Lord is pleased, this indeed is my boon: / let me have intense devotion to you, O eternal God."

1.127.s:
śrīsūrya uvāca
bhūyastuṣṭo'smi bhadraṃ te varaṃ varaya suvrata .
sa dvitīyaṃ varaṃ vavre tadaiva varadaṃ vibhum . . 26
1.127.d:
श्रीसूर्य उवाच
भूयस्तुष्टोऽस्मि भद्रं ते वरं वरय सुव्रत ।
स द्वितीयं वरं वव्रे तदैव वरदं विभुम् ॥ 26
1.127.m: The holy Sun said: / "I am greatly pleased; blessings upon you! Choose a boon, O you of noble vows." / He then chose a second boon from the all-pervading lord who grants boons:

1.127.s:
malaḥ śarīrasaṃstho me tvatprasādātpraṇaśyatu .
yena me śuddhamakhilaṃ vapurbhavatu gopate . . 27
1.127.d:
मलः शरीरसंस्थो मे त्वत्प्रसादात्प्रणश्यतु ।
येन मे शुद्धमखिलं वपुर्भवतु गोपते ॥ 27
1.127.m: Let the impurity abiding in my body perish by your grace, / so that my entire form may become pure, O lord of rays.

1.127.s:
sumanturuvāca
sa tathāstviti tenokto bhāskareṇa mahātmanā .
tāṃ mumoca rujaṃ sāmbo dehāttvacamivoragaḥ . . 28
1.127.d:
सुमन्तुरुवाच
स तथास्त्विति तेनोक्तो भास्करेण महात्मना ।
तां मुमोच रुजं साम्बो देहात्त्वचमिवोरगः ॥ 28
1.127.m: Sumantu said: / Told by him, the great-souled Bhāskara, "So be it," / Sāmba shed that affliction from his body like a snake its skin.

1.127.s:
tato rūpeṇa divyena rūpavānabhavatpunaḥ .
praṇamya śirasā devaṃ purato'vasthito'bhavat . . 29
1.127.d:
ततो रूपेण दिव्येन रूपवानभवत्पुनः ।
प्रणम्य शिरसा देवं पुरतोऽवस्थितोऽभवत् ॥ 29
1.127.m: Then, endowed with a divine form, he became handsome once again. / Bowing with his head to the god, he stood before him.

1.127.s:
śrīsūrya uvāca
bhūyaśca śṛṇu me sāmbaṃ tuṣṭo'haṃ yadbravīmi te .
adya prabhṛti tvannāmnā mama sthānāni suvrata . .
kṣitau ye sthāpayiṣyanti teṣāṃ lokāḥ sanātanāḥ . . 1.127.30
1.127.d:
श्रीसूर्य उवाच
भूयश्च शृणु मे साम्बं तुष्टोऽहं यद्ब्रवीमि ते ।
अद्य प्रभृति त्वन्नाम्ना मम स्थानानि सुव्रत ॥
क्षितौ ये स्थापयिष्यन्ति तेषां लोकाः सनातनाः ॥ 1.127.30
1.127.m: The holy Sun said: / "Listen further, O Sāmba, to what I, being pleased, say to you: / From this day forward, O you of noble vows, those who establish my sanctuaries / in your name upon the earth, theirs are eternal worlds.

1.127.s:
sthāpayasvaiva māmasmiṃścandrabhāgātaṭe śubhe .
tava nāmnā ca sāmbedaṃ parāṃ khyātiṃ gamiṣyati . . 31
1.127.d:
स्थापयस्वैव मामस्मिंश्चन्द्रभागातटे शुभे ।
तव नाम्ना च साम्बेदं परां ख्यातिं गमिष्यति ॥ 31
1.127.m: Establish me right here on this auspicious bank of the Candrabhāgā; / and under your name, O Sāmba, this [place] will attain supreme fame.

1.127.s:
kīrtistavākṣayā loke khyātiṃ yāsyati suvrata .
bhūyaśca te pradāsyāmi pratyahaṃ svapnadarśanam . . 32
1.127.d:
कीर्तिस्तवाक्षया लोके ख्यातिं यास्यति सुव्रत ।
भूयश्च ते प्रदास्यामि प्रत्यहं स्वप्नदर्शनम् ॥ 32
1.127.m: Your imperishable renown will attain celebrity in the world, O you of noble vows; / and moreover, I will grant you daily vision [of me] in dreams."

1.127.s:
sumanturuvāca
evaṃ dattvā varaṃ tasmai vṛṣṇisiṃhāya cāparam .
pratyakṣadarśanaṃ dattvā tatraivāntaradhāddhariḥ . . 33
1.127.d:
सुमन्तुरुवाच
एवं दत्त्वा वरं तस्मै वृष्णिसिंहाय चापरम् ।
प्रत्यक्षदर्शनं दत्त्वा तत्रैवान्तरधाद्धरिः ॥ 33
1.127.m: Sumantu said: / Having thus granted this boon and another to that lion of the Vṛṣṇis, / and having granted a direct vision [of himself], Hari vanished right there.

1.127.s:
ya idaṃ paṭhate stotraṃ trikālaṃ bhaktimānnaraḥ .
trisaptaśatamāvartya homaṃ vā saptarātrakam . . 34
1.127.d:
य इदं पठते स्तोत्रं त्रिकालं भक्तिमान्नरः ।
त्रिसप्तशतमावर्त्य होमं वा सप्तरात्रकम् ॥ 34
1.127.m: The devoted man who recites this hymn at the three junctures of the day, / having repeated it twenty-one times, or [performs] a burnt offering for seven nights,

1.127.s:
rājyakāmo labhedrājyaṃ dhanakāmo labhedadhanam .
rogārto mucyate rogādyathā sāmbastathaiva saḥ . . 35
1.127.d:
राज्यकामो लभेद्राज्यं धनकामो लभेदधनम् ।
रोगार्तो मुच्यते रोगाद्यथा साम्बस्तथैव सः ॥ 35
1.127.m: desiring a kingdom, would obtain a kingdom; desiring wealth, would obtain wealth; / afflicted by disease, he is released from disease just as Sāmba was.

1.127.s:
sūryalokaṃ vrajeccāpi bhaktyā pūjya divākaram .
ramate ca tathā tasmindevaiśca parivāritaḥ . . 36
1.127.d:
सूर्यलोकं व्रजेच्चापि भक्त्या पूज्य दिवाकरम् ।
रमते च तथा तस्मिन्देवैश्च परिवारितः ॥ 36
1.127.m: Having worshipped the Sun with devotion, he also goes to the world of the Sun, / and delights there, surrounded by the gods.

1.127.s:
iti śrībhaviṣye mahāpurāṇe brāhme parvaṇi saptamīkalpe sāmbopākhyāne sūryaprasādavarṇanaṃ
nāma saptaviṃśatyadhikaśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ . 127 .
sāmbastavavarṇanam
1.127.d:
इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराणे ब्राह्मे पर्वणि सप्तमीकल्पे साम्बोपाख्याने सूर्यप्रसादवर्णनं
नाम सप्तविंशत्यधिकशततमोऽध्यायः । 127 ।
साम्बस्तववर्णनम्
1.127.m:
Thus ends the one hundred and twenty-seventh chapter, named "Description of the Grace of the Sun" in the Sāmba narrative of the Saptamīkalpa, in the Brāhmaparvan of the glorious Bhaviṣya Mahāpurāṇa.
Description of the Hymn of Sāmba

1.128.s:
sumanturuvāca
astāvīcca tata sāmbaḥ kṛśo dhamanisantataḥ .
rājannāmasahasreṇa sahasrāṃśuṃ divākaram . . 1
1.128.d:
सुमन्तुरुवाच
अस्तावीच्च तत साम्बः कृशो धमनिसन्ततः ।
राजन्नामसहस्रेण सहस्रांशुं दिवाकरम् ॥ 1
1.128.m: Sumantu said: / Then, emaciated and with his veins protruding, Sāmba praised / the thousand-rayed Sun, the day-maker, with a thousand names, O King.

1.128.s:
khidyamānaṃ tato dṛṣṭvā sūryaḥ kṛṣṇātmajaṃ tadā .
svapne'smai darśanaṃ dattvā punarvacanamabravīt . . 2
1.128.d:
खिद्यमानं ततो दृष्ट्वा सूर्यः कृष्णात्मजं तदा ।
स्वप्नेऽस्मै दर्शनं दत्त्वा पुनर्वचनमब्रवीत् ॥ 2
1.128.m: Then, seeing Kṛṣṇa's son in distress, the Sun / granted him a vision in a dream and spoke these words again:

1.128.s:
śrīsūrya uvāca
sāmba sāmba mahāvāho śṛṇu jāmbavatīsuta .
alaṃ nāmasahasreṇa paṭha cemaṃ śubhaṃ stavam . . 3
1.128.d:
श्रीसूर्य उवाच
साम्ब साम्ब महावाहो शृणु जाम्बवतीसुत ।
अलं नामसहस्रेण पठ चेमं शुभं स्तवम् ॥ 3
1.128.m: The holy Sun said: / "Sāmba, Sāmba, O mighty-armed son of Jāmbavatī, listen: / enough with the thousand names; recite this auspicious hymn.

1.128.s:
yāni guhyāni nāmāni pavitrāṇi śubhāni ca .
tāni te kīrtiyiṣyāmi prayatnādavadhāraya . 4
1.128.d:
यानि गुह्यानि नामानि पवित्राणि शुभानि च ।
तानि ते कीर्तियिष्यामि प्रयत्नादवधारय । 4
1.128.m: Those names which are secret, purifying, and auspicious, / I will proclaim to you; bear them in mind with care:

1.128.s:
vaikartano vivasvāṃśca mārtaṇḍo bhāskaro raviḥ .
lokaprakāśakaḥ śrīmāṃllokacakṣurgraheśvaraḥ . 5
1.128.d:
वैकर्तनो विवस्वांश्च मार्तण्डो भास्करो रविः ।
लोकप्रकाशकः श्रीमांल्लोकचक्षुर्ग्रहेश्वरः । 5
1.128.m: Vaikartana, Vivasvat, Mārtaṇḍa, Bhāskara, Ravi, / illuminator of the worlds, the glorious, eye of the world, lord of the planets,

1.128.s:
lokasākṣī trilokeśaḥ kartā hartā tamisrahā .
tapanastāpanaścaiva śuciḥ saptāśvavāhanaḥ . 6
1.128.d:
लोकसाक्षी त्रिलोकेशः कर्ता हर्ता तमिस्रहा ।
तपनस्तापनश्चैव शुचिः सप्ताश्ववाहनः । 6
1.128.m: witness of the world, lord of the three worlds, the creator, the destroyer, dispeller of darkness, / the burner, the scorcher, pure, borne by seven horses,

1.128.s:
gabhastihasto brahmā ca sarvadevanamaskṛtaḥ .
ekarviśatirityeṣa stava iṣṭassadā mama . . 7
1.128.d:
गभस्तिहस्तो ब्रह्मा च सर्वदेवनमस्कृतः ।
एकर्विशतिरित्येष स्तव इष्टस्सदा मम ॥ 7
1.128.m: having rays for hands, Brahmā, and worshipped by all the gods. / This hymn of twenty-one [names] is always beloved to me.

1.128.s:
śarīrārogyadaścaiva dhanavṛddhiyaśaskaraḥ .
stavarāja iti khyātastriṣu lokeṣu viśrutaḥ . 8
1.128.d:
शरीरारोग्यदश्चैव धनवृद्धियशस्करः ।
स्तवराज इति ख्यातस्त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुतः । 8
1.128.m: It grants bodily health, increases wealth, and brings renown; / renowned as the 'King of Hymns', it is famous in the three worlds.

1.128.s:
ya etena mahābāho dve sandhye'stamanodaye .
stauti māṃ praṇato bhūtvā sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate .. 9
1.128.d:
य एतेन महाबाहो द्वे सन्ध्येऽस्तमनोदये ।
स्तौति मां प्रणतो भूत्वा सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते ॥ 9
1.128.m: Whoever, O mighty-armed one, bows down and praises me with this [hymn] at the two twilights, sunset and sunrise, / is freed from all sins.

1.128.s:
mānasaṃ vācikaṃ vāpi kāyikaṃ yacca duṣkṛtam .
ekajāpyena tatsarvaṃ praṇaśyati mamāgrataḥ . 1.128.10
1.128.d:
मानसं वाचिकं वापि कायिकं यच्च दुष्कृतम् ।
एकजाप्येन तत्सर्वं प्रणश्यति ममाग्रतः । 1.128.10
1.128.m: Whatever wrong action was committed mentally, verbally, or physically, / all that perishes before me by a single recitation.

1.128.s:
eṣa japyaśca homaśca sandhyopāsanameva ca .
balimantro'rghyamantro'tha dhūpamantrastathaiva ca . .11
1.128.d:
एष जप्यश्च होमश्च सन्ध्योपासनमेव च ।
बलिमन्त्रोऽर्घ्यमन्त्रोऽथ धूपमन्त्रस्तथैव च ॥11
1.128.m: This is a recitation, a burnt offering, and the twilight prayer itself, / as well as the mantra for offerings, the mantra for water oblation, and the mantra for incense.

1.128.s:
annapradāne snāne ca praṇipāte pradakṣiṇe .
pūjito'yaṃ mahāmantraḥ sarvapāpaharaḥ śubhaḥ . . 12
1.128.d:
अन्नप्रदाने स्नाने च प्रणिपाते प्रदक्षिणे ।
पूजितोऽयं महामन्त्रः सर्वपापहरः शुभः ॥ 12
1.128.m: In giving food, in bathing, in bowing down, and in circumambulation, / this great mantra, honoured, removes all sins and is auspicious."

1.128.s:
evamuktvā sa bhagavānbhāskaro jagatāṃ patiḥ .
āmantrya kṛṣṇatanayaṃ tatraivāntarhito'bhavat . . 13
1.128.d:
एवमुक्त्वा स भगवान्भास्करो जगतां पतिः ।
आमन्त्र्य कृष्णतनयं तत्रैवान्तर्हितोऽभवत् ॥ 13
1.128.m: Having spoken thus, the Blessed Lord Bhāskara, Lord of the worlds, / bid farewell to Kṛṣṇa's son and disappeared right there.

1.128.s:
sāmbo'pi stavarājena stutvā saptāśvavāhanam .
prītātmā nīrujaḥ śrīmāṃstasmādrogādvimuktavān . . 14
1.128.d:
साम्बोऽपि स्तवराजेन स्तुत्वा सप्ताश्ववाहनम् ।
प्रीतात्मा नीरुजः श्रीमांस्तस्माद्रोगाद्विमुक्तवान् ॥ 14
1.128.m: Sāmba too, having praised the one borne by seven horses with the 'King of Hymns', / gladdened at heart, free from illness, and glorious, was completely cured of that disease.

1.128.s:
iti śrībhaviṣye mahāpurāṇe brāhme parvaṇi saptamīkalpe sāmbastavavarṇanaṃ
nāmāṣṭāviṃśatyadhikaśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ . 128 .
sāmbakṛtādityamūrtisthāpanavarṇanam
1.128.d:
इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराणे ब्राह्मे पर्वणि सप्तमीकल्पे साम्बस्तववर्णनं
नामाष्टाविंशत्यधिकशततमोऽध्यायः । 128 ।
साम्बकृतादित्यमूर्तिस्थापनवर्णनम्
1.128.m:
Thus ends the one hundred and twenty-eighth chapter, entitled "Description of the Praise by Sāmba", in the Saptamīkalpa of the Brāhmaparvan in the venerable and great Bhaviṣyapurāṇa. 128.
Description of the Installation of the Image of Āditya by Sāmba

1.129.s:
sumanturuvāca
atha labdhavaraḥ sāmbo varaṃ prāpya purātanam .
manyamānastadāścaryaṃ prahṛṣṭenāntarātmanā . . 1
1.129.d:
सुमन्तुरुवाच
अथ लब्धवरः साम्बो वरं प्राप्य पुरातनम् ।
मन्यमानस्तदाश्चर्यं प्रहृष्टेनान्तरात्मना ॥ 1
1.129.m: Sumantu said: / Then Sāmba, having obtained his boon, receiving the ancient boon, / thinking it a wonder, with an inner self overjoyed,

1.129.s:
pūrvābhyāsena tenaiva sārdhamanyaistapasvibhiḥ .
snāpanārthaṃ nātidūraṃ candrabhāgāṃ nadīṃ yayau . . 2
1.129.d:
पूर्वाभ्यासेन तेनैव सार्धमन्यैस्तपस्विभिः ।
स्नापनार्थं नातिदूरं चन्द्रभागां नदीं ययौ ॥ 2
1.129.m: along with other ascetics, by that same previous habit, / went to the Candrabhāgā river, not very far away, to bathe.

1.129.s:
kṛtvātmamaṇḍalākāraṃ śraddadhāno dinedine .
sasnau sañcintayāmāsa kiṃ rūpaṃ sthāpayāmyaham . . 3
1.129.d:
कृत्वात्ममण्डलाकारं श्रद्दधानो दिनेदिने ।
सस्नौ सञ्चिन्तयामास किं रूपं स्थापयाम्यहम् ॥ 3
1.129.m: Having made the form of a solar disc, full of faith day after day, / he bathed and reflected: "What form shall I install?"

1.129.s:
sa snātaḥ sahasaivātha praṇamya1 tu prabhāvatīm .
uhyamānāṃ jalaughena pratimāṃ sammukhīṃ raveḥ . . 4
1.129.d:
स स्नातः सहसैवाथ प्रणम्य1 तु प्रभावतीम् ।
उह्यमानां जलौघेन प्रतिमां सम्मुखीं रवेः ॥ 4
1.129.m: Having bathed, bowing at once to the radiant [deity], / [he saw] an image facing the Sun, carried along by the stream of water.

1.129.s:
tāṃ dṛṣṭvā tasya vīrasya samutpannamidaṃ yathā .
devena yattadājñaptaṃ tadidaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ . . 5
1.129.d:
तां दृष्ट्वा तस्य वीरस्य समुत्पन्नमिदं यथा ।
देवेन यत्तदाज्ञप्तं तदिदं नात्र संशयः ॥ 5
1.129.m: Seeing it, this [thought] arose in that hero: / "What was commanded by the god, this is that, of this there is no doubt."

1.129.s:
sa tāmuttārya salilādānīya ca mahīpate .
tasminmitravanoddeśe sthāpayāmāsa tāṃ tadā . . 6
1.129.d:
स तामुत्तार्य सलिलादानीय च महीपते ।
तस्मिन्मित्रवनोद्देशे स्थापयामास तां तदा ॥ 6
1.129.m: Pulling it out from the water and bringing it, O lord of the earth, / he then installed it in that region of Mitravana.

1.129.s:
nidhāya pratimām̐lloke sāmbastasya mahātmanaḥ .
mitraṃ mitravane ramye sthāpayitvā vidhānataḥ . . 7
1.129.d:
निधाय प्रतिमाम्̐ल्लोके साम्बस्तस्य महात्मनः ।
मित्रं मित्रवने रम्ये स्थापयित्वा विधानतः ॥ 7
1.129.m: Having set up the image in the world, Sāmba, / having installed Mitra of that great soul properly in pleasant Mitravana,

1.129.s:
tatastāmeva papraccha praṇamya pratimāṃ raveḥ .
keneyaṃ nirmitā nātha bhavato hyākṛtiḥ śubhā . . 8
1.129.d:
ततस्तामेव पप्रच्छ प्रणम्य प्रतिमां रवेः ।
केनेयं निर्मिता नाथ भवतो ह्याकृतिः शुभा ॥ 8
1.129.m: bowing down, then asked that very image of the Sun: / "By whom, O Lord, was this auspicious form of yours fashioned?"

1.129.s:
pratimā tamuvācātha śṛṇu sāmba bruve svayam .
nirmitā yena cāpyeṣā madīyā puruṣākṛtiḥ . . 9
1.129.d:
प्रतिमा तमुवाचाथ शृणु साम्ब ब्रुवे स्वयम् ।
निर्मिता येन चाप्येषा मदीया पुरुषाकृतिः ॥ 9
1.129.m: The image then said to him: "Listen, Sāmba, I shall tell you myself / by whom this human form of mine was fashioned.

1.129.s:
mamātitejasāviṣṭaṃ rūpamāsītpurātanam .
asahyaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ tato'smyabhyarcitaḥ suraiḥ . .
sahyaṃ bhavatu te rūpaṃ sarvaprāṇabhṛtāmiti . . 1.129.10
1.129.d:
ममातितेजसाविष्टं रूपमासीत्पुरातनम् ।
असह्यं सर्वभूतानां ततोऽस्म्यभ्यर्चितः सुरैः ॥
सह्यं भवतु ते रूपं सर्वप्राणभृतामिति ॥ 1.129.10
1.129.m: My ancient form was permeated with excessive brilliance, / unbearable to all beings; therefore I was entreated by the gods: / 'Let your form become bearable to all living beings.'

1.129.s:
tato mayā samādiṣṭo viśvakarmā mahātapāḥ .
tejasāṃ śātanaṃ kurvanrūpaṃ nirvartayasva me . . 11
1.129.d:
ततो मया समादिष्टो विश्वकर्मा महातपाः ।
तेजसां शातनं कुर्वन्रूपं निर्वर्तयस्व मे ॥ 11
1.129.m: Then Viśvakarman of great austerity was commanded by me: / 'Paring away the brilliance, fashion my form.'

1.129.s:
tatastu matsamādeśāttenaiva nipuṇaṃ tadā .
śākadvīpe bhramiṃ kṛtvā rūpaṃ nirvartitaṃ mama . . 12
1.129.d:
ततस्तु मत्समादेशात्तेनैव निपुणं तदा ।
शाकद्वीपे भ्रमिं कृत्वा रूपं निर्वर्तितं मम ॥ 12
1.129.m: Then, by my command, my form was skillfully fashioned / by him at that time, placing me upon the lathe in Śākadvīpa.

1.129.s:
prītyā teṣāṃ prapañco'yaṃ sa mayā kāritaḥ punaḥ .
teneyaṃ kalpavṛkṣāttu nirmitā viśvakarmaṇā . . 13
1.129.d:
प्रीत्या तेषां प्रपञ्चोऽयं स मया कारितः पुनः ।
तेनेयं कल्पवृक्षात्तु निर्मिता विश्वकर्मणा ॥ 13
1.129.m: Out of affection for them, this expansion was caused by me again; / by him, Viśvakarman, this was fashioned from the wish-granting tree.

1.129.s:
kṛtvā himavataḥ pṛṣṭhe purā siddhaniṣevite .
tvadarthaṃ candrabhāgāyāṃ tatastenāvatāritā . . 14
1.129.d:
कृत्वा हिमवतः पृष्ठे पुरा सिद्धनिषेविते ।
त्वदर्थं चन्द्रभागायां ततस्तेनावतारिता ॥ 14
1.129.m: Having fashioned it formerly on the ridge of the Himavat frequented by Siddhas, / it was then brought down into the Candrabhāgā by him for your sake.

1.129.s:
bhavatastāraṇārthaṃ hi tataḥ sthānamidaṃ śubham .
ruciraṃ sarvadā sāmba sānnidhyaṃ me'tra yāsyati . . 15
1.129.d:
भवतस्तारणार्थं हि ततः स्थानमिदं शुभम् ।
रुचिरं सर्वदा साम्ब सान्निध्यं मेऽत्र यास्यति ॥ 15
1.129.m: Indeed, for your deliverance, this place is auspicious; / pleasing, O Sāmba, my presence here will remain always.

1.129.s:
sānnidhyaṃ mama pūrvāhṇe sutīre drakṣyate janaiḥ .
kālapriye ca madhyāhne'parāhṇe cātra nityaśaḥ . . 16
1.129.d:
सान्निध्यं मम पूर्वाह्णे सुतीरे द्रक्ष्यते जनैः ।
कालप्रिये च मध्याह्नेऽपराह्णे चात्र नित्यशः ॥ 16
1.129.m: My presence will be seen by people in the forenoon at Sutīra, / at midday at Kālapriya, and in the afternoon always here.

1.129.s:
pūrvāhṇe pūjayed brahmā madhyāhne cakradhṛtsvayam .
śaṅkaraścāparāhṇe tu māṃ pūjayati sarvadā . . 17
1.129.d:
पूर्वाह्णे पूजयेद् ब्रह्मा मध्याह्ने चक्रधृत्स्वयम् ।
शङ्करश्चापराह्णे तु मां पूजयति सर्वदा ॥ 17
1.129.m: In the forenoon Brahmā worships me; at midday the Wielder of the Discus himself; / and in the afternoon Śaṅkara always worships me."

1.129.s:
ityukto'sau bhagavatā bhāskareṇa sa yādavaḥ .
harṣamāpa mahābāho bhāskaro'ntardadhe tataḥ . . 18
1.129.d:
इत्युक्तोऽसौ भगवता भास्करेण स यादवः ।
हर्षमाप महाबाहो भास्करोऽन्तर्दधे ततः ॥ 18
1.129.m: Having been spoken to thus by the blessed Sun, that Yādava / attained joy, O mighty-armed one; then the Sun disappeared.

1.129.s:
iti śrībhaviṣye mahāpurāṇe brāhme parvaṇi saptamīkalpe sāmbopākhyāne
sāmbakṛtādityamūrtisthāpanaṃ nāmaikonatriṃśadadhikaśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ . . 129 .
prasādalakṣaṇavarṇanam
1.129.d:
इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराणे ब्राह्मे पर्वणि सप्तमीकल्पे साम्बोपाख्याने
साम्बकृतादित्यमूर्तिस्थापनं नामैकोनत्रिंशदधिकशततमोऽध्यायः ॥ 129 ।
प्रसादलक्षणवर्णनम्
1.129.m:
Thus ends the one hundred and twenty-ninth chapter, entitled "Installation of the Image of Āditya by Sāmba", in the narrative of Sāmba, in the Saptamīkalpa of the Brāhmaparvan in the venerable and great Bhaviṣyapurāṇa. 129.
Description of the Characteristics of a Temple

1.130.s:
śatānīka uvāca
